items.title: Overlooked biodiversity hotspots revealed by a pluralistic approach for quantifying amphibian biodiscovery needs
items.summary_raw: Undocumented and poorly known species spanning Linnean and Wallacean biodiversity shortfalls pose a major challenge to conservation due to the uncertainty they introduce. To address this, we developed a novel pluralistic approach that accounts for sampling gaps, spatial patterns, environmental associations, and varying conservation needs simultaneously, using amphibians as a case study. Using environment-based richness models and species accumulation curves (SACs), we identified areas with high biodiscovery needs for amphibians. These were concentrated primarily in humid tropical South America, sub-Saharan Africa, and East/Southeast Asia. While environmental models produced more reliable richness estimates than SACs overall, SAC-based estimates nonetheless added unique insights, especially in biodiverse, moderately well-sampled areas like Costa Rica and Panama. By integrating environmental models and SACs—thus leveraging combined strengths of previous approaches—our holistic scoring technique also proved consistent in estimating biodiscovery priorities across ecoregions, enabling robust recommendations for future sampling.

items.title: Anthropocentric comparisons with human language impede our understanding of whale communication
ACSS2 modulates endothelial glycolysis in angiogenesis
items.summary_raw: Endothelial cells (ECs) sustain high glycolytic flux and display remarkable metabolic plasticity. Although molecular pathways regulating endothelial glycolysis are well characterized, metabolic mechanisms underlying hypoxia-induced glycolytic activation during angiogenesis remain poorly understood. Here, we show that acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2) serves as a critical metabolic modulator, coupling acetate utilization with glycolytic flux to control EC function and angiogenesis. The high level of ACSS2-mediated acetate-to-acetyl-CoA conversion in angiogenic front ECs sustains acetyl-CoA levels, which are essential for EC proliferation and retinal vascularization. Conversely, endothelial-specific Acss2 deletion disrupts pathological angiogenesis and normalizes tumor vasculature. Mechanistically, ACSS2 maintains hypoxia-inducible factor 1α transcriptional activity and stabilizes glucose transporter 1, thereby preserving glycolysis. Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 knockdown rescues metabolic and functional defects in ACSS2-deficient ECs, revealing the vital role of acetyl-CoA homeostasis in modulating hypoxic endothelial metabolism. Taken together, these data establish ACSS2 as a pivotal regulator of vascular development and suggest that targeting acetate metabolism may be an effective way to modulate pathological angiogenesis.

items.title: Galectin-3 links microglial neuroinflammation to Aβ aggregation and lysosomal processing
items.summary_raw: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaque-associated microglial responses, linking Aβ aggregation, lysosomal function, and neuritic pathology. Using postmortem brain tissue from AD patients, we found that Gal3 + microglia preferentially associate with cored plaques and correlate with increased LAMP1 + dystrophic neurites. Gal3 was also detected in microglial lysosomal compartments, extramicroglial dystrophic structures, and in association with extracellular amyloid fibrils, suggesting roles in both intracellular and extracellular Aβ processing. In APP mice, Gal3 deficiency reduced plaque burden and neuritic dystrophy, increased plaque compaction, and enhanced TREM2 coverage around amyloid plaques. Mechanistically, in vitro microglial experiments showed that Gal3 modulates Aβ uptake and lysosomal processing, whereas lysosomal dysfunction promoted the accumulation of fibrillar Aβ from initially monomeric species, particularly in Gal3-deficient cells. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Gal3 preferentially binds fibrillar Aβ, inhibits secondary nucleation, and alters fibril morphology, while Gal3-modified fibrillar Aβ reduces N2a neuronal cell number. Finally, in silico structural analyses identified candidate Gal3 interactors enriched in leucine-rich-repeat and immunoglobulin-like…

items.title: Language model teams as distributed systems
items.summary_raw: Large language models (LLMs) are growing increasingly powerful. Yet, fundamental constraints on the reasoning, memory, and performance of individual models has sparked recent interest in scaling abilities using LLM teams. With growing deployment of LLM teams at scale, there is a need for principled guidelines for when teams help, how many agents to use, and how structure impacts performance. Rather than building these teams through trial-and-error, we propose using distributed systems as a formal foundation for designing and evaluating LLM teams. Under this formal framework, we derive predictions about how task structure and team architecture should shape performance. Empirical evidence supports these predictions: LLM team scaling follows classical distributed computing laws based on the structure of a task, and centralized and decentralized architectures exhibit the asymmetric vulnerabilities predicted by distributed systems theory. These results establish distributed computing as a generative framework that yields testable, quantitative predictions about LLM team behavior and informs the construction of more efficient and capable teams.

items.title: Biological stochasticity increases the evolutionary limit of lifespan
items.summary_raw: The mutation accumulation theory attributes aging to the decline in selection strength with age. While classical models assume fixed ages of mutation expression, empirical evidence reveals significant interindividual variation in the timing of mutation expression. Here, we develop mathematical models incorporating this stochasticity. By tracking the fate of lethal mutations, we characterize the boundary of the “selection shadow” where genetic drift overcomes purging selection against such mutations—a fundamental evolutionary limit, termed the lifespan drift barrier, setting a theoretical benchmark for the pace of aging. Our results show that for both stochastic age- and state-dependent mutations, variation in the age of mutation expression generally pushes back this lifespan drift barrier. This outcome is a universal consequence of the inherent convexity of the selection gradient under extrinsic mortality: early expression in a subset of individuals intensifies purging selection, thereby raising the drift barrier. In addition, we demonstrate that while this variance shifts this evolutionary threshold (determining the pace of aging), it leaves the mortality trajectory at mutation–selection balance (the shape of aging) fundamentally unaltered. These findings thus help explain how the pace and shape of aging can become uncoupled.

items.title: Paul R. Ehrlich: Visionary pioneer and public scientist for nature and humanity
items.summary_raw: Paul R. Ehrlich is legendary for his scientific insight and impact—and even more so for bringing science to the public through writing, speaking, and, most famously, twenty-some appearances on the Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson. He was quick-witted—he would readily add quick-tempered, with chagrin—and could bring down a house. Paul cherished deep friendships and nature. He loved collaborating with his wife of 71 years, Anne H. Ehrlich, and with innumerable students and colleagues all over the world. He made transformative contributions of astonishing range, including in ecology and evolution, biodiversity and conservation, human population and overconsumption, and the integration of ecology and economics. He was deeply committed to racial and social justice, reflected in his actions and writing.

items.title: Structural basis for the selective inhibition of the PI3KC3-C2 complex by Rubicon in endolysosome maturation and mitophagy
items.summary_raw: Rubicon is a negative regulator of autophagy and the endolysosomal network (ELN) and an antagonist of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex II (PI3KC3-C2). Inhibition of Rubicon is considered a potential means to therapeutically upregulate autophagy and the ELN to treat Parkinson’s disease and other conditions characterized by autophagic and ELN dysfunction. Rubicon is specific for the UV radiation resistance-associated gene protein (UVRAG)-containing PI3KC3-C2 over the purely autophagic ATG14-containing PI3KC3-C1 complex. Here, we determined the high-resolution cryoelectron microscopy structure of PI3KC3-C2 in complex with the PI3KC3-binding domain of Rubicon and compared it to cryo-EM structures of unbound PI3KC3-C2 and PI3KC3-C1. Rubicon binds directly to PI3KC3-C2 only via the BARA domain of the BECN1 subunit, which is common to both C1 and C2. The selectivity of Rubicon for the PI3KC3-C2 complex over the PI3KC3-C1 complex is attributed to a conformation of the BECN1 BARA domain induced by UVRAG, rather than to direct contact with UVRAG or direct antagonism by the ATG14 subunit of PI3KC3-C1. Targeted disruption of the Rubicon:PI3K3-C2 structural interface by site-directed mutations enhances mitophagic activity in human epithelial cells to levels comparable to those observed in Rubicon knockout cells. Similarly, disruption of the interaction in Rubicon-overexpressing hippocampal neurons restored lysosomal flux to wild-type levels. These data show that…

items.title: Neuronal IL-34 programs microglial activity via the TGF-β–MEF2C axis to constrain neuroinflammation following brain ischemia
items.summary_raw: Brain ischemia induces robust neuroinflammation driven by microglial activation, yet whether ischemic neurons actively reprogram microglial phenotypes to limit inflammation remains elusive. Here, we identify neuronal interleukin-34 (IL-34) as a critical immunomodulatory signal that maintains microglial homeostasis after cerebral ischemia. We demonstrate that ischemic injury augments IL-34-CSF1R signaling between neurons and microglia. Neuron-specific overexpression of Il34 (Syn1- Il34 tg mice) attenuated infarct volume and neurodeficits after middle cerebral artery occlusion, whereas neuronal Il34 knockdown exacerbated brain injury. Microglial depletion abolished IL-34-mediated neuroprotection, suggesting microglia as essential effectors. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that neuronal IL-34 preserved homeostatic microglial signatures ( P2ry12, Cx3cr1, Tgfbr1 ), while suppressing inflammatory activities ( Il1b, Tnf, Cxcl2 ) through upregulation of the transcription factor MEF2C. Mechanistically, IL-34 activated TGF-β signaling in microglia and inhibition of TGF-β signaling abolished the protective effects of IL-34, whereas microglia-specific Mef2c overexpression rescued neuroprotection despite TGF-β blockade. Thus, ischemic neurons deploy IL-34 to orchestrate the immunoregulatory activity of microglia via the TGF-β–MEF2C axis, representing a previously unrecognized endogenous mechanism counteracting neuroinflammation. Our study reveals neuronal IL-34 as a potential…

items.title: Chaperone modulation and the structural basis for sRNA recognition by the conserved ribonuclease YicC
items.summary_raw: The broadly conserved bacterial endoribonuclease YicC represents a widespread but enigmatic family of RNA processing enzymes with poorly defined substrate selectivity. Here, we show that Escherichia coli YicC displays a distinct selectivity, cleaving small regulatory RNAs (sRNAs) such as RyhB and RprA but not when they are in complexes with cognate mRNA targets or RNA sponges. Furthermore, we demonstrate that RyhB processing is modulated, but not abolished, by the RNA chaperone Hfq. Our cryo-EM structures of E. coli YicC in apo form and in complexes with substrate and nonsubstrate RNA species capture marked quaternary and tertiary structural switches triggered by sRNA stem-loop binding that engulf and ratchet the RNA into an internal catalytic channel. Structural comparison of cleavable (RyhB) and noncleavable (MicA) sRNA-bound complexes reveal a near-identical ground-state binding mode, proving that cavity docking is sequence-tolerant and decoupled from catalytic execution. Together, our findings suggest that YicC may be a state-selective endoribonuclease and reveal a framework for selective RNA clearance in bacterial posttranscriptional regulation.

items.title: Local influenza forecasts outperform state-level forecasts in the United States
items.summary_raw: Accurate outbreak forecasts are critical for timely and effective public health response. In the United States, however, most forecasts are produced at the state level, which can mask substantial substate heterogeneity and limit their utility for local planning. We generated and evaluated forecasts of the percentage of Emergency Department visits attributable to influenza across 173 large metropolitan Health Service Areas (HSAs) using a gradient boosting quantile regression model and compared their accuracy to forecasts derived from state-level data alone. At a 1-wk, 2-wk, and 3-wk horizon, local forecasts outperformed state-based forecasts in 98.8%, 90.8%, and 78.6% of HSAs, respectively, achieving mean weighted interval scores that were on average a 39.2% lower (95% range: 5.9 to 76.7%), 19.6% lower (−6.3 to 59.5%), and 11.4% lower (−11.7 to 44.9%), respectively. The performance advantage of local forecasting was strongest in HSAs representing a smaller share of their state’s population and increased with the proportion of the HSA population living in urban areas and the number of metropolitan areas within a state. These results, based on an analysis of HSAs with populations greater than 250,000, demonstrate that fine-scale modeling can substantially improve forecast accuracy and highlight the potential value of local forecasts for outbreak preparedness and response.

items.title: Four phases and temporal threshold of population calcium response during locomotion in cortical astrocytes
items.summary_raw: Calcium activity is a major form of astrocyte excitability. Astrocytic calcium events arise spontaneously and in response to behavior, but how unitary events shape population-level activity remains unclear. Using two-photon imaging in the primary somatosensory cortex of awake mice running on a freely rotating disk, we analyzed calcium dynamics during quiescence and locomotion. During quiescence, population fluctuations were driven mainly by the co-occurrence of new events rather than by their enlargement. During locomotion, responses progressed through four phases: emergence of new events, their merging into a superevent, fragmentation, and an afterburst. These responses combined the progressive recruitment of active regions with amplification of a reproducible spatial calcium pattern. New events emerged within the first seconds after locomotion onset, indicating a rapid astrocytic response. A full population response required about 5 s of locomotion: Shorter episodes failed to develop the superevent and produced markedly smaller responses. In suprathreshold episodes, the superevent displayed a reproducible ΔF/F pattern. Hotspots within this pattern had shorter latencies and were also more active during quiescence. A dynamic mode decomposition with control model driven by synthetic or real locomotion inputs reproduced the response phases, temporal threshold, and superevent pattern. These findings show that locomotion-evoked astrocytic calcium activity is an ordered…

items.title: Localized end-on heating for hot spot ignition in precompressed isochoric plasmas
items.summary_raw: In fast ignition inertial confinement fusion, a “heating cone” is employed to shorten the transport distance of the relativistic electron beam (REB) to the high-density plasma core, thereby mitigating energy losses at the plasma edge. However, its insertion depth and survival time are constrained by the sustained pressure from the large-scale plasma edge during the implosion process. Our whole-process simulations demonstrated that, in the double-cone ignition scheme, the head-on collision of two deuterium-tritium plasma jets not only forms a high-density plateau with a small-scale edge, but also substantially reduces the interaction time between the heating cone and the colliding plasma to approximately 0.1 ns . This shortened interaction time enables the heating cone to remain intact after the peak compression, even when placed directly at the small-scale edge of the colliding plasma. The small-scale edge is compatible with the range of the soft-spectrum REB generated by the heating lasers. Such a REB efficiently heats a localized end-on hot spot adjacent to the high-density plateau, guided by a kT-level magnetic field amplified from a seed field during the collision process. Ignited by the localized hot spot, the high-density plateau can undergo sufficient burning and achieve a fusion energy gain of 6.8 using 60 kJ heating lasers.

items.title: An ensemble of functionally distinct factors enables spatial quality control during proteasome base assembly
items.summary_raw: The proteasome is an essential mediator of the ubiquitin–proteasome system and a complex molecular machine. Hallmarks of de novo proteasome assembly include dedicated chaperones and many subunits, culminating into major assembly intermediates such as the base. Emerging evidence suggests that proteasome assembly is subject to extensive quality control (QC). To understand mechanisms of QC, we examined a crucial assembly checkpoint during base assembly. Our findings reveal sequential mechanisms of QC, in which a checkpoint complex is first assembled, then sequestered into the nucleus, away from ongoing proteasome assembly in the cytoplasm. Assembly of this checkpoint complex depends on noncanonical ubiquitination of the Nas2 chaperone. The Nas2 ubiquitin chain functions as a scaffold by binding the Rpn13 ubiquitin receptor, which is distantly positioned within the same complex. Rpn13 also positions the ubiquitin chain to its neighboring Hul5 ubiquitin ligase, for continual chain elongation to further stabilize this complex. Ubiquitin-mediated assembly enables spatial sequestration of this checkpoint complex through its intrinsic nuclear localization signal (NLS). This NLS on Rpt4 specifically targets this checkpoint complex into the nucleus, emphasizing the importance of spatial compartmentalization. Our findings reveal that proteasome assembly integrates multiple functionally distinct components as QC factors (1 assembly chaperone, 2 ubiquitin regulators, and 1 NLS) to…

items.title: CD49f identifies stem-like memory T cells with enhanced therapeutic potency
items.summary_raw: The efficacy of adoptive cell therapies depends on the presence of T cells with durable self-renewal, proliferative capacity, and differentiation potential, yet heterogeneity within starting cell populations remains a major barrier to consistent clinical outcomes. Here, we identify CD49f as a marker of a unique subset of human memory T cells with stem-like characteristics. CD49f Hi memory CD8 + and CD4 + T cells exhibited transcriptional and phenotypic features associated with T cell stemness, including elevated LEF1, TCF1, CCR7, CD27, and CD28, while CD49f Lo cells exhibited effector-like transcriptional programs. Clinical evaluation of solid-organ transplant recipients treated with virus-specific T cells for cytomegalovirus complications demonstrated that autologous T cell therapies manufactured from CD49f Hi -enriched T cells were associated with superior immune reconstitution and greater in vivo expansion of CMV-specific T cells. Functional assays further revealed that CD49f Hi memory T cells possessed enhanced proliferative capacity and transcriptional plasticity following activation. Consistent with these findings, CD19 CAR T cells engineered from CD49f Hi memory T cells demonstrated improved persistence and conferred superior survival in a preclinical lymphoma model. Together, these findings establish CD49f as a marker of a stem-like memory T cell subset with enhanced therapeutic potential and identify CD49f Hi enrichment as a practical strategy to improve the…

items.title: Basal radial glia abundance and morphotype diversity in the hippocampal dentate gyrus imply their evolutionarily ancient origin
items.summary_raw: Basal radial glia (bRG) are neural progenitor cells (NPCs) essential for primate neocortical expansion, but their presence in other brain regions and across species remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the developing mouse dentate gyrus (DG), unlike the neocortex, harbors abundant NPCs that transcriptionally and morphologically resemble human neocortical bRG. This striking abundance is conserved across other Boreoeutherian species, including mice, marmosets, ferrets, and pigs. Comparative transcriptomics uncovered a shared morphoregulatory gene signature between bRG in mouse DG and human neocortex. Immunohistochemical analysis showed diversity in DG bRG morphotypes across species. Remarkably, compared to the neocortex, DG bRG consistently exhibit greater morphotype diversity. Ancestral state reconstruction suggests that this diversity was already present in the common ancestor of Boreoeutherians. Together, our findings position the DG as a conserved, evolutionarily ancient niche for bRG, revealing that region- and species-specific adaptations of NPCs extend beyond the neocortex.

items.title: Niche constraints drive differences between mycorrhizal fungal guilds in future range shifts
items.summary_raw: Mycorrhizal fungi are a diverse and ubiquitous group of plant symbionts whose distribution strongly influences ecosystem function across the globe. Yet, until now, we do not have quantitative data on the range sizes of different mycorrhizal fungal taxa, limiting our capacity to forecast future shifts in community composition and function. Here, we use 115,924 DNA sequence-derived observations to map the distribution of 651 common mycorrhizal fungal taxa and forecast future changes to their range sizes. We demonstrate that climate, plant cover, and soil factors, particularly mean annual temperature, net primary productivity, and soil organic carbon, exert major control over mycorrhizal fungal distributions. Based on these drivers, the ecological niches of mycorrhizal fungi consistently differ between arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal functional guilds. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal taxa generally occupy a wider niche breadth than ectomycorrhizal fungi, occurring across larger ranges of climate, soil, plant cover, topography, and disturbance conditions. Our models also predict widespread decreases in the suitable range size of mycorrhizal fungal taxa under projected future global climates, with average ranges decreasing by 13.8% or ~2.2 million km 2 under high emissions scenarios (ssp5-8.5). This decrease in projected range size will be most pronounced for ectomycorrhizal fungi, strongly linked to constraints from their smaller overall niches. By generating a global atlas of…

items.title: A periplasmic regulator establishes adaptive impermeability to control carbapenem entry
items.summary_raw: Outer-membrane permeability is a major determinant of antibiotic susceptibility in Gram-negative bacteria and is generally thought to be controlled through transcriptional regulation of porin expression. Here we identify the small periplasmic protein PtrA as a regulator of OprD-dependent carbapenem permeability in Pseudomonas aeruginosa . PtrA promotes imipenem resistance without altering OprD abundance, associates with OprD-containing membrane complexes and reduces intracellular imipenem entry. Using zinc and copper as complementary physiological signals, we show that PtrA-mediated permeability control is mechanistically distinct from CzcRS-dependent repression of oprD and precedes transcriptional porin depletion. These findings define a two-phase mechanism in which rapid periplasmic regulation provides an immediate adaptive response before transcriptional remodeling of the outer membrane. Our work identifies adaptive impermeability as a previously unrecognized mechanism linking environmental sensing to dynamic control of bacterial outer-membrane permeability.

items.title: In brief | 18 November '26
They migrated to New York for work. Now they’re fighting to climate-proof it.
items.summary_raw: Earlier this year, riding his e-bike through New York City’s bustling streets on a sweltering July afternoon, José Yos began to smell smoke. It wasn’t coming from a nearby burning building or a beat-up yellow cab. Instead, the smell came from hundreds of miles away in Canada. Raging wildfires in Quebec had sent a cloud of thick, smoky air toward the city, blanketing it in a strange orange haze. It wasn’t the first time Yos, a 40-year-old from Guatemala who delivers food and groceries on apps like DoorDash, had experienced this. In 2023, Canada had its worst wildfire season on record, with around 37 million acres (15 million hectares) of land going up in flames. Wildfire smoke traveled down from Quebec to New York , polluting the air and turning the skies a deep shade of orange . This summer, though, the city was also in the middle of a heat emergency — its second in as many weeks. The temperature was projected to reach close to 100 degrees Fahrenheit that day, and the heat index — the day’s real feel temperature — was supposed to be even higher. In response to the extreme weather double whammy, the city had sent cooling vans around the city, opened additional cooling centers and urged New Yorkers to stay home, ideally in air conditioning. But Yos was on the clock. He couldn’t afford to go home or take a real break. He had reserved his hours on Uber Eats a week in advance and was worried that if he took longer than usual to fulfill orders, his in-app rating would go down…

items.title: What Congress’ bill to speed up energy projects would mean for you
items.summary_raw: The largest renewable energy project ever built in the United States — the sprawling SunZia wind farm and power line in New Mexico — took two decades to build. Its transmission line, necessary to transport the wind power to cities in Arizona and California, faced opposition from birders, the military, and tribes. While some disputes were resolved, tribes’ concerns about the project’s impacts on historic sites have remained unsettled, leading to court battles that still haven’t been resolved even though the line was completed in June. Such legal challenges commonly delay renewable energy projects and the transmission lines that carry their power to population centers. The threat of lawsuits and resistance from utilities have driven down long-distance power line construction in the United States, limiting the country’s ability to use cheap renewable energy. The Senate passed a “permitting reform” bill this week that could make it much faster and easier to build transmission lines and renewable energy projects — but it casts a wide net, easing construction for almost all large infrastructure projects. Supporters of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act , or BAAJA — including clean energy companies and prominent climate-conscious senators — argue the bill is necessary to clean up the power grid. Critics say it could disempower communities, tribes, and environmental groups while also speeding construction of fossil fuel infrastructure. The bill still needs to pass…

items.title: In Utah, a ‘hydrocarbon highway’ could run right through this petroglyph-filled canyon
items.summary_raw: Federal land managers call it “the world’s longest art gallery,” a Utah red-rock canyon full of ancient petroglyphs, Native American panels, and pioneer-era inscriptions written in axle grease. Earlier this year, the Trump administration approved plans to blast a “ hydrocarbon highway ” connecting nearby oil fields to rail-loading facilities through Nine Mile Canyon’s cultural and archaeological-rich sites. Last month environmental and historic preservation groups sued to stop them. “It’s like constructing a highway through the Louvre Museum,” said J. Michael Hansen, president of the Nine Mile Canyon Coalition, in a statement. The Trump administration resurrected the project in eastern Utah after it stalled out during President Joe Biden’s term. Plaintiffs in the lawsuit say approvals for the highway bypassed the normal public comment and ecological review processes. The Nine Mile Canyon Coalition, the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance, and the Center for Biological Diversity filed their complaint in Utah’s U.S. District Court against the Department of Interior and Bureau of Land Management. Nine Mile Canyon runs about 46 miles. Plans call for dynamiting, paving, and widening a road through Gate Canyon, a tributary to Nine Mile, which has 47 historic sites of its own with 43 eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, according to BLM documentation from 2015. The proposed highway would cut through 5.3 miles of land owned by both the Bureau of Land Management and…

items.summary_raw: Growing recognition of the interdependence between human health, climate change and environmental sustainability has highlighted the importance of understanding how climate-friendly behaviours can simultaneously promote individual health, climate and environmental protection. Concepts such as One Health, Planetary Health and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) emphasize that human well-being depends on healthy ecosystems, a stable climate and supportive social systems. Yet achieving these goals remains challenging because many climate-friendly behaviours involve trade-offs between short-term individual benefits and long-term collective outcomes. This Special Issue addresses these challenges at the intersection of SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and SDG 13 (Climate Action). The contributing papers span topics including mobility, nutrition, climate emotions, self-regulation, social norms and behaviour-change interventions. Collectively, the papers demonstrate that health and climate outcomes are deeply interconnected but that co-benefits are conditional on psychological mechanisms, social contexts and structural opportunities. Based on this evidence, we propose an integrative framework linking environmental conditions, psychological processes and behavioural responses, as well as health and climate outcomes for researchers, practitioners and policy-makers. To achieve SDG 3 and SDG 13 together, psychology must promote well-being not as an end point in itself but as a…

items.title: Low-carbon building research into practice: insights from Australia
items.summary_raw: Purpose Low-carbon buildings play an important role in achieving net-zero carbon targets. Real-world implementation of carbon reduction strategies in the building sector is underexplored. Numerous technologies and strategies have been proposed to reduce building-related carbon emissions. However, their practical adoption within the construction industry is not well understood. Therefore, this study investigates current carbon reduction practices within the Australian construction industry and provides insights into the acceleration of net-zero carbon targets globally. Design/methodology/approach A list of low-carbon technologies that could be adopted in buildings was first identified through a critical literature review. An online questionnaire survey was then distributed among Australian construction professionals to investigate their practical adoption. Descriptive and frequency analyses were performed on the 73 valid survey responses with the diffusion of innovations theory providing the key theoretical foundation. Findings The findings reveal that most low-carbon strategies are implemented at a moderate level within the Australian construction sector. Energy-efficient technologies, such as LED lighting and HVAC systems, are the commonly used practices. The adoption of passive technologies, low-carbon materials and renewable energy systems ranges from rare to moderate levels, while carbon estimating practices are the least implemented. Originality/value This is one of the…

items.title: Assessing policy-supported soil and water conservation measures using a refined, field-scale connectivity-based SWAT+ framework
items.summary_raw: Climate change is increasing the frequency of hydrological extremes, requiring effective conservation measures to reduce soil erosion and improve soil water management. This study evaluated policy-supported conservation measures in a Hungarian agricultural catchment using a field-explicit, connectivity-based SWAT+ framework. Unlike conventional HRU-based representations, in which HRUs do not retain the spatial adjacency of individual fields, the COCOA setup preserves fields as contiguous model units and represents the directed routing of surface runoff and lateral subsurface flow between adjacent fields. This allows conservation measures to influence not only treated fields but also hydrologically connected downslope fields through management-induced changes in water fluxes. The connectivity-based framework was combined with field-specific management representation and parameterised for policy-supported conservation measures, enabling their effects to be evaluated under spatially explicit, field-scale conditions. The effectiveness of the simulated measures was evaluated using indicators of streamflow, soil moisture, soil loss by water erosion and arable land loss, expressed as relative changes compared with baseline management. Strategically placed erosion control strips reduced soil loss across agricultural land by 7–8% despite occupying only a small proportion of the landscape. No-tillage combined with cover crops and conversion of arable land to grassland were the most…

items.title: Political orientation, conspiracy mentality, and climate misinformation exposure and belief: An examination of indirect associations
items.summary_raw: Conspiracy theories about climate change are often linked to lower public trust in science and weaker support for mitigation policies. Yet, little is known about how ideological dispositions are associated with exposure to climate misinformation (the type of content that individuals are likely to encounter) and belief in these narratives. This cross-sectional study examined these aspects in an Italian sample (N = 460). Participants filled in questionnaires assessing political orientation, conspiracy mentality, and belief in climate change conspiracy theories, and provided self-report measures estimating exposure to, and belief in, widely circulating climate misinformation. Path analyses showed that a more right-wing political orientation was associated with both a generalized conspiratorial mindset and specific climate-related conspiracy beliefs. Most importantly, a theoretically driven model in which the latter variables accounted for indirect associations between political orientation and climate misinformation exposure and belief showed a good fit to the empirical data. These findings highlight the complex relations that link ideological orientation and conspiratorial beliefs to vulnerability to climate change misinformation, emphasizing the need for interventions that foster informed debate.

items.title: Evaluation of age differences in climate policy support among Republicans voters
items.summary_raw: One of the primary barriers to implementing climate change policy within the United States is opposition from Republican politicians and voters. For decades, Republican opposition to climate policy has been underpinned by disbelief in anthropogenic climate change. In recent years, however, Republican belief in anthropogenic climate change and support for climate policy have meaningfully increased. Recent research indicates that younger Republicans are more likely to support climate policy than older Republicans, and that the relationship between age and policy support is stronger for Republicans than for Democrats. We argue that differences between older and younger Republicans are partially a result of differences across three factors: climate anxiety, experiences with extreme weather, and more negative attitudes toward capitalism. To explore these dynamics, we apply a series of regression analyses to a large non-probability sample of Republicans (n = 1,249). Results show all three factors to be significant, although the importance of each individual factor shifts by age bracket, indicating the existence of different cognitive and affective frameworks across cohorts. We argue that these findings portend the potential for a realignment of climate politics and the weakening of the partisan climate gap moving forward.

items.title: Scenario-based forecasting of carbon sequestration and oxygen production in urban green spaces using i-Tree forecast: a case study of Sidoarjo, Indonesia
items.source_name: Journal of Environmental Health Science and Engineering
items.summary_raw: Transportation is the largest CO2 emission contributor in Indoneisa, followed by industries, waste management, and households. The major greenhouse gas has seen carbon offsetting attempts with varying proposals, one of which is by implementing Green Open Spaces (GOS), acting as ecological buffers, carbon sinks, and oxygen producers. This study evaluates existing greenery at Abhirama Park (urban core) and Apkasi Park (suburban area) in Sidoarjo Regency (East Java, Indonesia), Utilizing tree planting scenarios to assess CO2 sequestration and oxygen production changes. The methodology integrates field base inventories, vegetation density analysis (GIS-based NDVI), microclimate observations, and i-Tree Forecast modelling from three scenarios (existing conditions, instant greening, and gradual greening). Observations ran for two weeks on select days (Monday, Friday, Sunday) at specific times (Morning, Midday, and Evening) to observe diurnal variatons. The results show Abhirama Park having more complex vegetation structure with a higher tree count (159 trees vs 70 trees), greater carbon sequestration capacity (2.14 tons/year to 0.92 tons/year) compared to Apsaka park. Sequestration values reveal extremely limited capacity of carbon offset abilities from both parks for each respective locations, accounting only 1.33% and 0.5% of total emissions. items.title: Whose voices are counted? survey sampling and public preferences for energy decarbonization
items.source_name: Journal of Environmental Studies and Sciences
items.summary_raw: Public acceptance of technologies used to decarbonize the electric grid can shape efforts to reduce climate risks. However, estimates of public preferences may depend on how survey respondents are recruited, raising questions about whether different sampling approaches yield comparable results. We compare five survey sampling approaches—three designed to produce nationally representative samples and two convenience samples—to assess demographic representativeness and preferences for grid-decarbonization technologies. The convenience samples were highly nonrepresentative and produced skewed estimates of public support that were not corrected by weighting. Among the nationally representative approaches, opt-in online sampling with quotas most closely resembled 2022 American Community Survey demographics. The three nationally representative approaches produced broadly similar energy-preference profiles in this study, although some technology-specific differences remained. Address-based sampling and random-digit dialing yielded similar preference profiles, while the opt-in sample showed statistically higher support for on-land wind and lower support for offshore wind and solar farms. Across these samples, rooftop solar ranked first, followed by solar farms, while nuclear and fossil fuels with carbon sequestration ranked last; the random-digit-dial sample differed by ranking offshore wind last. These findings demonstrate tradeoffs among survey sampling approaches: convenience…

items.title: The Perceived Role of Prosumer Energy in the Sustainable Energy Transition: Evidence from Rural Municipalities in Poland
items.summary_raw: The energy transition requires not only the development of renewable energy sources but also the active participation of local communities in energy production and consumption processes. In this context, prosumer energy is increasingly recognised as a key component of the sustainable energy transition. Despite the growing body of research on prosumerism, relatively little attention has been devoted to how its significance is perceived by local authorities, particularly in rural areas. The aim of this article is to identify how representatives of rural municipalities in Poland perceive the role of prosumer energy in the sustainable energy transition. The study employed a survey-based research design involving representatives of 518 rural municipalities. The analysis encompassed five dimensions of the energy transition: (1) the achievement of environmental and climate objectives, (2) energy justice, (3) environmental responsibility, (4) value conflicts, and (5) local communities’ energy resilience. The findings indicate that prosumer energy is perceived as an important component of the sustainable energy transition in rural areas. Respondents attribute particular significance to its contribution to environmental protection, the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, the strengthening of energy security, and the enhancement of local communities’ resilience to energy crises. At the same time, the results reveal a clear asymmetry in perceptions of prosumer energy, with…

items.title: What drives sustainable fashion behaviour: fashion interest and environmental attitudes
items.summary_raw: Introduction: The fashion industry is among the most resource-intensive and polluting consumer sectors, and consumer behavior is central to reducing its environmental impact. Although research has extensively examined pro-environmental attitudes, it has treated fashion interest inconsistently, often assuming it conflicts with sustainability despite evidence that sustainable consumers can be highly fashion-conscious. This study examines how environmental attitudes and fashion interest relate to clothing behavior across the consumption cycle, distinguishing three behavioral types: sufficiency (buying less, keeping garments longer), care and efficiency (maintenance, repair, lower-impact laundering), and circular and reuse (second-hand acquisition and diverting used clothing from disposal). Materials and methods: Drawing on an online survey of 2000 Canadian consumers, we measured fashion interest using standardized scales. We regressed each of 27 ordinal outcomes on the two attitudes using ordered logistic regression; reported odds ratios per standard deviation, with and without demographic controls; and verified results with Brant tests, generalized ordered logit models, and false-discovery-rate correction. Results: The two attitudes function as distinct motivational orientations, with associations that vary systematically by behavioral type. Environmental attitude is positively associated with sustainable behavior across all three types and is unaffected by demographic…

items.title: Demographic ageing and household energy poverty in China: the moderating roles of digital access and social capital
items.summary_raw: Background As demographic ageing progresses, increasing attention has been paid to ensuring access to basic energy services for households with older members and understanding their potential vulnerability. Household energy affordability is essential for maintaining basic living standards, health, and well-being. Existing studies have examined the relationships between population ageing, household life cycles, and household energy poverty. However, whether the association between demographic ageing and energy poverty varies according to household digital access, social capital, and resource conditions remains unclear. Methods Based on data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) 2022, this study uses a Logit model to examine the association between demographic ageing and household energy poverty, tests the moderating roles of digital access and social capital, and conducts heterogeneity analyses across household groups. Results Demographic ageing is significantly positively associated with household energy poverty. A 10-percentage-point increase in demographic ageing is associated with an average increase of approximately 1.27 percentage points in the predicted probability of households falling into energy poverty. Propensity score matching and multiple robustness checks provide additional support for this finding. Digital access and social capital weaken the positive association between demographic ageing and household energy poverty. This association is significantly…

items.title: Staging Survival: Public Performance and Cosmologies of Climate Change in India’s Sundarbans Delta
items.summary_raw: This article explores emergent cosmologies of climate change in a predominantly Dalit Hindu community in the Sundarbans of West Bengal, India. In recent years, my interlocutors have begun to link changing weather patterns to human activity, often through reference to divine and demonic beings. This article considers how public performances generate such cosmological shifts. I argue that performance offers a key modality through which ecological cosmologies have been constituted in the Sundarbans historically and through which they are now transforming. This reflects performance’s world-making qualities, namely, its capacity to create more-than-human presence, evoke subjunctive realities, and transmit moral visions. I consider two performative genres: jatra, a form of open-air theater, and NGO performances addressing anthropogenic climate change. Organizing Ecological Sustainability Policy: The Craft and Professional Norms of Policy Professionals
items.summary_raw: Despite numerous national and international goals, public policies often prove unsuccessful in stopping sustainability crises. Policy professionals are central in formulating and implementing sustainability policy. To understand how these policies come to be, and why they often fall short, it is also important to understand the craft and professional norms that constitute the professionalism of policy professionals working on ecological sustainability policy. We combine the descriptive perspectives of public administration with the more prescriptive perspectives of sustainability research literature to bring into focus what these professionals do, and what they do not. Based on 40 interviews with Dutch policy professionals, we find that the crafts they use are mostly adapted to the uncertainty and contestedness of wicked sustainability issues, while their professional norms are still in line with those laid out by Weber at the beginning of the 20th century. To deal with the wickedness, the crafts of organizing knowledge and expertise, organizing interests and framing are important for dealing with political distance. Norms respondents refer to represent mostly a traditional image of neutrality of civil servants. This dominance of neutrality as a norm also shows in how respondents do not see a role for themselves in initiating sustainability policy, and we theorize that this is an underexplored possible explanation for why sustainability policies so often fail to deliver. items.title: A Study on Differences in Death Attitudes Among Family Caregivers
items.source_name: The Journal of Medicine Humanity and Media
items.summary_raw: Despite the vast number of family caregivers in China, this group has long been systematically overlooked. As a critical variable in caregiving communication and ethical decision-making, their views on life and death have yet to be systematically examined from a typological perspective. This study aims to uncover the underlying typological structure of Chinese family caregivers' perspectives on life and death, thereby providing an empirical foundation at the conceptual level for developing differentiated caregiving support systems. Utilizing the Q-methodology, this study recruited 20 family caregivers as participants. A set of 66 statements regarding perspectives on life and death was developed and analyzed using principal component factor analysis via the PQ Method software to identify the quantity and structure of subjective cognitive types. Furthermore, in-depth interviews were conducted to interpret and name each identified type. Three stable typologies of perspectives on life and death were identified: (1) The Goal-Oriented Type, which takes family relationships as its core anchor, cherishes life without denying death, and maintains a clear sense of self-boundaries; (2) The Secular Anti-Traditional Type, which takes individual sovereignty as its ethical starting point, opposes the meaningless prolongation of life, and emphasizes the autonomous construction of meaning amidst absurdity; (3) The World-Affirming Relational Type, which is grounded in collective ethics…

items.title: Exploring Individual Factors Contributing to Trauma-Informed Attitudes in Law Enforcement Personnel
items.source_name: Journal of Police and Criminal Psychology
items.summary_raw: Over the past 20 years, public trust in law enforcement has declined, with a sharp decrease following the 2020 murder of George Floyd. In response, agencies have increasingly turned to trauma-informed care (TIC) to rebuild community relationships. Individual officer characteristics may influence the adoption of trauma-informed practices, particularly emotional intelligence and intellectual humility. This study surveyed 127 police officers from a Southwestern U.S. state to examine relationships between emotional intelligence, intellectual humility, and trauma-informed attitudes. Analyses showed intellectual humility and emotional intelligence were significantly and positively related to trauma-informed attitudes. Implications for officer wellbeing, training, and development are discussed.

items.title: Joined Up Landscapes: Embedding Nature‐Based Solutions in UK Food Systems for Climate Adaptation
items.summary_raw: Food and land systems in the United Kingdom face growing challenges from climate change, biodiversity loss, and ongoing uncertainty regarding transitions to Net Zero. Nature-based Solutions (NbS) offer a promising way to address these issues, providing co-benefits for climate adaptation, food production, and ecosystem restoration. However, the implementation of NbS remains fragmented, unstrategic, and underfunded. The interdisciplinary Joined Up Landscapes (JUL) research project, funded by UKRI and Defra, aims to strengthen the contribution of NbS to climate adaptation in the context of UK food systems. This article presents an outline of the JUL project. JUL is structured around five interconnected work packages alongside three case studies demonstrating a range of agricultural NbS, including wetlands, floodplain mosaics, and catchment-scale habitat restoration. Preliminary findings highlight the importance of local context, stakeholder engagement, and flexible funding. JUL aims to inform policy, empower practitioners, and support a more climate-resilient UK food system.

items.title: Understanding the impact of persuasion techniques in climate change mis- and disinformation
items.summary_raw: Fabricators of disinformation may strategically exploit people's susceptibility to emotive information and cognitive biases to make false narratives more persuasive. In an online experiment, we presented a representative sample of 5,121 participants from Germany, France, Ireland, Italy, and Poland with both false and true climate change statements. We explored the effect of seven widely used persuasion techniques (appeal to authority, black-and-white fallacy, sowing doubt, name-calling, thought-terminating cliché, bandwagon, and loaded language) on agreement with and perceived persuasiveness of both types of statements. Preregistered analyses revealed an overall negative effect of persuasion techniques on agreement, driven primarily by reduced agreement with true claims. The effect of persuasion techniques on false claims varied by technique: Appeals to authority and the black-and-white fallacy increased agreement with false claims relative to true claims, while name-calling and thought-terminating cliché decreased agreement with both. Contrary to expectations, people with extreme climate change beliefs were more strongly influenced by persuasion techniques. Findings provide insights into the role of persuasion techniques in false information, improving understanding of how such techniques operate and where their influence is limited.

items.title: NARRATIVAS DA CRISE CLIMÁTICA: ANÁLISE DO DISCURSO DA COBERTURA JORNALÍSTICA SOBRE EVENTOS EXTREMOS
items.summary_raw: Enchentes, secas e chuvas extremas ocupam o noticiário brasileiro com frequência crescente, e a forma como a imprensa conta esses eventos define o que o público entende como causa e quem é chamado a responder pelo dano. Este artigo pergunta se a cobertura jornalística de eventos climáticos extremos, sobretudo a brasileira, os narra como desastres naturais isolados ou como manifestações da crise climática, com quais recursos discursivos e atribuindo causa e responsabilidade a quem. A análise reúne estudos de discurso e de enquadramento sobre a cobertura de crises hídricas, inundações e tempestades, e os confronta com estudos sobre vulnerabilidade e governança dos desastres no Brasil. Nos casos brasileiros examinados, a imprensa de referência narra os eventos como episódios centrados no dano e no instante de maior destruição, com a natureza como explicação suficiente e com silêncio sobre a gestão, a adaptação e os atingidos. O vínculo com a crise climática aparece em picos breves de atenção após grandes eventos e numa moldura de consenso científico e soluções técnicas. Nos dois enquadramentos, a causa tende ao impessoal. Quando há agentes, aparecem como adversários políticos ou, em veículos independentes, como governos e empresas. A leitura em dois eixos, escala temporal e agência da causa, mostra que a passagem da natureza ao clima não garante, por si só, a responsabilização.

Civil Nuclear Energy Cooperation between China and Central Asia amid the Energy Transition: Drivers, Institutional Constraints, and Policy Pathways
items.source_name: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
items.summary_raw: This article examines how energy transition goals, industrial complementarity, partner diversification, and institutional capacity shape civil nuclear energy cooperation between China and Central Asian countries. It develops a three-level framework covering national demand, international political economy, and institutional conditions, and proposes a nested comparison of Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Publicly documented cooperation in nuclear fuel manufacturing and nuclear safety regulation illustrates distinct channels of engagement. The available evidence supports a research design and preliminary case descriptions; it does not yet establish the proposed causal mechanisms or the outcomes of planned nuclear power projects. The article specifies observable indicators, process-tracing tests, and policy implications for cooperation under international safety standards.

items.title: A toolkit for countering climate misinformation
The Dhaka Manifold: Operationalising Liquid Legitimacy through Institutional Bricolage and Sheaf-Theoretic Governance in Climate-Vulnerable Voids
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: The decomposition of the Westphalian order into a landscape of Permanent Systemic Instability calls for governance architectures capable of continuous, algorithmic and topological adaptation. The Liquid Legitimacy framework holds that polycentric stakeholding, continuous cryptographic audit trails, narrative resilience protocols and explicit custodianship of the Reserve of Humanity are the mechanisms that generate durable consent within fluid institutions. Operationalising these mechanisms in the Global South, where institutional voids, vast urban informality and severe climate vulnerability dominate, demands a theoretical extension. This paper extends the framework by synthesising Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety, Amari's information geometry, the sheaf-theoretic tradition of Curry, Ghrist and Spivak, and Cleaver's critical institutionalism. Using the megacity of Dhaka, Bangladesh, as its case, it argues that the so-called institutional voids of informal settlements such as Korail and Geneva Camp are not governance vacuums but dense topologies of institutional bricolage, evidenced by recent fieldwork on water, sanitation and hygiene through the 5As lens. Framing these informal, highly adaptive arrangements as local sheaf sections shows how the state can amplify its regulatory variety without resorting to coercive territorial monopoly. items.summary_raw: In spite of some loud voices both for and against it, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act has so far cruised through the Senate. That could change as soon as today as lawmakers begin to consider amendments ahead of a final vote. One of the main outstanding issues is how the bill’s changes to the National Historic Preservation Act would affect tribal sovereignty. Nevada Senator Catherine Cortez Masto, a Democrat, warned before the initial motion to proceed on the proposed legislation last week that she would not vote for the final bill unless lawmakers struck that section entirely. Since then, nearly 30 Democrats have signed onto an amendment proposed by California Senator Adam Schiff that would do just that. Republican senator Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma has also reportedly sought changes to the bill that would clarify some of the language without stripping it. The debate over the NHPA primarily concerns a process known as a Section 106 review.
