items.title: The debt burden of tropical cyclones and climate change
items.summary_raw: Addressing climate change through mitigation and adaptation is expected to require more than $6 trillion in global investment annually by 2035. Yet many countries face significant barriers to accessing this finance, including low or absent credit ratings, large debt burdens, and high borrowing costs. Climate change may further amplify these barriers, creating a “vicious cycle” in which mounting economic losses reduce the capacity of countries to invest in adaptation and mitigation. We provide evidence that the cost and availability of capital for many countries have already been shaped by both historical exposure to naturally-occurring tropical cyclones (TCs) and anthropogenic warming. Our empirical estimates suggest that, on average across TC-exposed countries, 20% of debt-to-GDP ratios are attributable to TCs from 1980 to 2019. Across all countries, GDP levels are on average 12% lower due to the combined impacts of baseline naturally-occurring TCs and anthropogenic warming. In a separate correlational machine-learning analysis, we estimate that these macroeconomic impacts are associated with an increased likelihood of hotter countries receiving credit ratings below investment grade ( < BBB–), as well as persistent credit risk premiums of at least 1 basis point in 64 countries and 5 basis points in highly exposed countries. We provide estimates for 181 countries, including many TC-affected and/or hot countries that do not have bond yield data. Future increases in…

items.title: Durable CD8-mediated remission after brief anti-HIV-1 antibody treatment requires FcγR engagement
items.summary_raw: Despite highly efficacious antiretroviral therapy (ART), durable ART-free remission remains a central objective of HIV-1 cure strategies. The randomized, placebo-controlled RIO trial recently demonstrated that long-acting broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies (bNAbs) can sustain prolonged virologic control after ART interruption, including control that persisted beyond the period of therapeutically relevant antibody concentrations, providing clinical evidence consistent with host-mediated suppression. However, the mechanisms underlying these “vaccinal” effects remain unresolved. Here, we establish Fcγ receptor (FcγR) engagement as an essential driver of multiyear remission after bNAb therapy in simian-human immunodeficiency virus (SHIV)-infected macaques. Brief therapy during acute infection with Fc domain variants of the bNAb 3BNC117, matched for antigen binding, neutralizing activity, and pharmacokinetics but differing in FcγR engagement, produced comparable early virologic control yet profoundly divergent long-term outcomes. Sustained CD8 T cell–dependent suppression lasting nearly 300 wk developed in every evaluable animal receiving the FcγR-engaging variant but arose in only one of eight recipients of the FcγR-null variant. FcγR-driven immunomodulation imprinted a CD8 T cell response characterized by enhanced antigen-specific effector function, early clonal focusing with sustained clonotype persistence, and distinct cellular-state transcriptional signatures. Our…

items.title: The sound of persuasion: Using generative AI to identify gender gaps in political influence
items.summary_raw: Women often experience a deficit in persuasive influence, particularly in contexts like politics, where expectations about women’s behavior may conflict with gendered expectations about the domain and role. In spite of this widespread pattern, the mechanisms behind the gender gap in persuasion are difficult to isolate and test in dynamic political conversations. Women may be less persuasive simply because role-based expectations prompt others to afford women less authority when speaking about politics generally or about some political topics. Alternatively, women may be less persuasive because they tend to use linguistic patterns or rhetorical strategies that are less effective. Using an original AI-based approach, we put 4,300 human subjects into realistic, real-time phone conversations with an AI agent. These agents were randomly assigned either a masculine or feminine gendered conversation topic and a male- or female-sounding voice, allowing us to manipulate topic and perceptions of speakers’ gender while holding constant other elements of rhetorical content and strategy. After validating the experimental treatments, we find no direct effects of perceived gender of the AI agent, as cued by voice. However, gender affects other important aspects of the persuasive interaction. Research subjects were more likely to be persuaded about the masculine topic (defense spending) than the feminine topic (aid to the poor). Additionally, women research subjects were, on average, more…

items.title: Activation of ROPGEFs by a malectin-like receptor kinase is involved in tip growth regulation in Physcomitrium patens
items.summary_raw: Rho-type GTPases of plants (ROPs) play essential roles in polarized cell growth, cell division, and organogenesis. Their activation depends on two types of guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs): the plant-specific PRONE-domain-containing ROPGEFs and DOCK-type SPKGEFs. While ROPGEFs have been proposed to be autoinhibited in pollen and activated by receptor-like kinases (RLKs), the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Using the moss Physcomitrium patens , we show that moss ROPGEF4 and ROPGEF6 exhibit low intrinsic GEF activity and are not autoinhibited by non-PRONE regions, whereas the catalytic domain of SPK1 and SPK6 is highly active. Through a candidate screen, we identified MLRK1, a malectin-like receptor kinase, as a ROPGEF-interacting protein. MLRK1 directly phosphorylates ROPGEF4 and ROPGEF6 and stimulates their GEF activities in vitro. These effects are attenuated by substituting key phosphosites (Ser231 in ROPGEF4 and Ser524/Thr526 in ROPGEF6) with nonphosphorylatable residues. Structural modeling, pull-down assays, and functional analyses indicate that phosphorylation enhances ROPGEF-ROP interactions and promotes the membrane localization of ROPGEF4/6. Furthermore, ROPGEFs are not essential for polarized cell growth on their own but act redundantly with SPK2. At the apical membrane, ROPGEFs appear to activate ROPs, reduce their diffusion, promote actin filament assembly and vesicle secretion, and ultimately facilitate cell expansion and growth…

items.title: Single-molecule FRET at 30: Toward conformational sequencing
items.summary_raw: Single-molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer (smFRET) turned 30 this year. We argue that three advances usually treated as separate endeavors, i.e., high-information-content per-molecule readout, sequence-linked massive parallelism, and automated trajectory decoding, are in fact one convergence that is turning smFRET from a one-molecule-at-a-time measurement into a high-throughput conformational sequencer, a platform that measures dynamic conformational phenotypes across sequence space at scale. This perspective traces the 30-y arc, forecasts which advances will prove most transformative over the next decade, states the conditions on which that forecast depends, and identifies the bottlenecks that still remain.

items.title: Local interactions drive hyperuniform tissue coverage during development
items.summary_raw: In living tissues, branched cells must efficiently cover territories to perform essential functions ranging from neural signaling to immune surveillance. However, how cells collectively establish and optimize tissue-scale coverage without global regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a biophysical theory of interacting branched cells and show that coupling their growth to neighbor repulsion drives efficient tissue tiling with minimal territorial overlap. Strikingly, our model predicts that the same local mechanism progressively suppresses long-range density fluctuations during development, driving the system toward a large-scale order called hyperuniformity. We confirm these theoretical predictions on microglial patterning in the developing retina and show that in perturbation experiments with limited arbor growth, both tiling and fluctuation suppression are disrupted. Our results reveal that two seemingly distinct features of tissue organization, efficient space-filling and large-scale order, share a single dynamical origin, suggesting a general principle for robust tissue patterning.

items.title: Neurovascular protein half-lives in health and aging
items.summary_raw: Specializations of blood vasculature in the central nervous system (CNS), including the blood–brain barrier (BBB), neurovascular coupling, and perivascular spaces, maintain CNS homeostasis and become dysfunctional in disease and aging. Protein turnover, the process by which proteins are continually degraded and replaced, profoundly influences cell and tissue function and is dysregulated in aging and disease. Understanding the turnover of neurovascular proteins could provide insight into how the vasculature achieves both long-term structural stability and dynamic regulation. Vascular proteins, however, are underrepresented in previous studies of in vivo brain protein turnover. In this work, we used stable isotope labeling, nonenzymatic blood vessel enrichment, and high-resolution mass spectrometry-based proteomics to quantify the half-lives of brain vascular proteins in young adult and aged mice. We report half-life estimates for 1,358 proteins, including components of endothelial junctions, BBB transporters, astrocyte endfoot proteins, and vascular basement membrane proteins. We found that certain classes of proteins with related functions had similar half-lives, including BBB junctional proteins (~3 d), BBB transporters (~2 to 6 d), and most basement membrane components (>30 d). We also identified peptide motifs enriched in proteins with short and long half-lives and found differences in half-life distributions for cell type–specific proteomes. Finally, although we did not…

items.title: Intrinsically disordered ligands for the control of receptor uptake by endocytosis
items.summary_raw: Endocytosis plays a crucial role in signaling, recycling, and degradation of receptors. Controlling endocytosis of specific receptors is therefore a major goal for both basic science and medicine. While antibody-induced dimerization can drive signaling-induced uptake of some receptors, the steric bulk of antibodies generally inhibits endocytosis, such that control over receptor uptake remains an unmet need. Recent work has demonstrated that attractive interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins drive inward membrane curvature, a key step in endocytosis. To harness this phenomenon for the control of receptor uptake, we designed chimeras that consisted of disordered domains fused to ligands for specific receptors. These chimeras condensed on membrane surfaces, in agreement with computational modeling, driving receptor clustering and uptake via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. In contrast, chimeras that repelled one another resisted condensation, helping receptors escape endocytosis and remain on the cell surface. Taken together, these results suggest that by modulating the amino acid sequence of intrinsically disordered ligands, we can promote or hinder the internalization of specific receptors by endocytic pathways. More broadly, these findings suggest a generalizable strategy for controlling the plasma membrane lifetime of diverse receptors, opening up new pathways for modulating cellular behavior and delivering therapeutics.

items.title: Structural insights into inhibition and activation mechanisms of plant calcium-dependent protein kinases
items.summary_raw: Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) comprise the major group of Ca 2+ -regulated kinases in plants and protists. These enzymes comprise an N-terminal kinase domain and a C-terminal Ca 2+ -dependent activation domain (CAD). We solved the crystal structures of autoinhibited and activated forms of a plant CDPK, Arabidopsis CPK3. In the autoinhibited form, the CAD resembles a “dumbbell-like” calmodulin protein with a long helix in the N terminus that inhibits the kinase domain in a pseudo-substrate manner. Upon Ca 2+ binding to the four EF-hands, CAD undergoes a dramatic conformational change with a rotation around the kinase domain, thus exposing its active site for substrate recognition. Our structural and biochemical studies reveal that most plant CDPKs may involve distinct mechanisms of activation compared with CDPKs from the apicomplexan parasites.

items.title: Competitive disruption of COI1 receptor assembly by a hemibiotrophic bacterial effector suppresses jasmonate-mediated immunity
items.summary_raw: Hormone pathways are central hubs in plant immunity, and their receptors, the critical initiators of signaling cascades, are logical targets of pathogen effectors. The jasmonic acid (JA) pathway is a cornerstone of defense against phytopathogens, especially necrotrophs. However, whether pathogens can directly target its receptor COI1 to subvert this defense layer has remained unclear. Here, we show that JA signaling positively regulates resistance to the devastating hemibiotrophic pathogen Ralstonia solanacearum and identified a bacterial effector, RipBO, that directly targets COI1 to counteract this defense. RipBO binds with high affinity to the F-box domain of COI1, competitively disrupts the COI1-ASK interaction, and thereby blocks SCF COI1 complex assembly. This disruption effectively stabilizes JAZ repressors and paralyzes JA-mediated immunity. Our findings clarify the contribution of JA signaling to bacterial wilt resistance and identify direct targeting of the hormone receptor as a pathogen virulence strategy, pointing to a potential vulnerability for crop protection.

items.title: Visualization of actin filaments in Plasmodium falciparum blood cell stages
items.summary_raw: The actin cytoskeleton is crucial to regulate cellular processes and morphology in eukaryotes, yet the tools to visualize it are not compatible with all organisms. In the apicomplexan Plasmodium falciparum , actin filaments are thought to be short and unstable, complicating their visualization. Here, we show that a tandem fusion of the actin-chromobody can label filaments in all P. falciparum red blood cell stages and observe actin structures in live cells with high spatiotemporal resolution. This work suggests that previous lack of labeling was due to suboptimal probes and that malaria blood stages have a filamentous and highly dynamic actin network.

items.title: Endosomal mRNA transport coordinates local mitochondrial bioenergetics during polar fungal growth
items.summary_raw: Mitochondrial function relies on the precise spatial coordination of protein synthesis and import. Most mitochondrial proteins are nuclear-encoded and must be supplied across varying intracellular distances. In highly polarized cells such as fungal hyphae and neurons, active long-distance mRNA transport is thought to sustain distal mitochondrial function, but its mechanistic coupling to protein import and organelle physiology is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that endosomal transport of mRNAs encoding mitochondrial proteins orchestrates local bioenergetics in infectious hyphae of Ustilago maydis . Using the subunit Atp3 of electron transport chain Complex V as a model, we uncover that the endosomal mRNA transporter Rrm4 is required for efficient mitochondrial protein import, particularly at growth poles. Loss of Rrm4 leads to defects in mitochondrial import, resulting in altered physiology. We propose that endosome-coupled mRNA transport constitutes a fundamental layer of subcellular mitochondrial homeostasis, with implications extending from fungal pathogenicity to neuronal disease.

items.title: Acetate–FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis
items.summary_raw: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are required for the protective effects of acetate, which are also dependent on FFAR2 signaling and IL-22. Neutrophil-specific deletion of FFAR2 impairs IL-22 responses, increases epithelial damage, and exacerbates colitis, while administration of recombinant IL-22 is sufficient to restore acetate protection in this context. Analysis of human ulcerative colitis biopsies reveals increased FFAR2 + neutrophils correlating with IL-22-related gene signatures. These findings indicate that acetate–FFAR2–neutrophil–IL-22 axis modulates intestinal inflammation, revealing a metabolic mechanism that links microbiota-derived signals to mucosal protection and highlighting potential therapeutic targets for inflammatory bowel diseases.
authors: Arilson Bernardo dos Santos Pereira Gomes

items.title: Anomeric configuration encodes mesophase preference of glucosylceramides in phospholipid membranes
items.summary_raw: Glycosphingolipids are key components of the cell glycocalyx, yet the extent to which their anomeric configuration affects their membrane organization remains unclear. Glucosylceramide (GlcCer) exists as α- and β-anomers with distinct biological activities, while the biophysical basis for these differences is unknown. Here, using nitroxide spin-labeled analogs of α- and β-GlcCer, we examined how the glycosidic stereochemistry affects their partitioning in phospholipid bilayers. In 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine, dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine, and distearoylphosphatidylcholine liposomes, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra of both probes contained two components: a broad, motion-restricted component consistent with GlcCer incorporated into the lamellar lipid bilayer and a sharp, highly mobile component attributed to some segregated, bilayer-associated GlcCer-rich nano-assemblies. EPR spectral simulations and complementary analyses showed that α-GlcCer predominantly partitioned into the lamellar phospholipid phase, whereas β-GlcCer was strongly enriched in the segregated GlcCer-rich phase. Importantly, analogous anomer-dependent EPR behavior was also observed for aqueous GlcCer dispersions in the absence of phospholipids, indicating that the distinct assembly propensities are intrinsic to the glycolipids and are modulated, rather than created, by the phospholipids. These findings support a two-mesophase model in which anomeric configuration acts as a…

items.title: Resilient j = 3/2 superconductivity in topological semimetal YPtBi
items.summary_raw: Cooper pairing in most of the known fermionic superfluids occurs via spin-1/2 quasiparticle interactions that lead to spin-singlet or spin-triplet pairing. In the topological semimetal YPtBi, strong spin–orbit coupling results in a band inversion between highly symmetric s - and p -like electronic bands and a degeneracy at the Γ point that ensures the manifold of j = 3/2 quasiparticle states thrive near the Fermi level, where superconducting pairing occurs. Here we study the effects of magnetic and nonmagnetic disorder and carrier density on this exotic superconducting pairing state. By varying levels of disorder and carrier densities by nearly two and three orders of magnitude, respectively, we show that the superconducting critical temperature of YPtBi has a remarkable robustness, with little variation across this span. Our results suggest that superconductivity in YPtBi may reside in a regime where phase stiffness, rather than pair formation, governs the transition temperature. The insensitivity of Cooper pairing to dramatic changes in quasiparticle environment in a j = 3/2 superconductor highlights a form of protection realized in topological high-spin superconductors.

items.title: Unconventional modulation of Na v 1.4 by a scorpion toxin through cooperative binding to voltage sensor and the pore domain
items.summary_raw: Voltage-gated sodium (Na v ) channels are targeted by animal peptide toxins, which serve as powerful molecular probes for dissecting channel structure-function relationships and lead molecules for drug discovery. β-scorpion toxins trap voltage sensor domains to remodel Na v channel gating, yet high-resolution structural evidence defining this process remains elusive. Here, we characterize LmNaTx1, a β-scorpion toxin from Lychas mucronatus . LmNaTx1 exerts state-dependent bimodal modulation on Na v 1.4: it facilitates channel activation while suppressing sodium conductance, accelerates slow-inactivation onset, and delays recovery from slow inactivation. We solved the 2.68 Å cryo-EM structure of the LmNaTx1-hNa v 1.4 complex, revealing that LmNaTx1 inserts into the extracellular cleft jointly formed by domain II voltage sensor (VSD II ) and the extracellular loop III (ECL III ) of the pore domain. Toxin binding remodels the S3–S4 II loop and displaces S0/S3 II helices to trap VSD II within a pre-activated intermediate state. MD simulations recapitulate step-wise VSD II conformational transitions and demonstrate that toxin-driven rearrangements tighten the intracellular pore gate. Mutagenesis combined with electrophysiology confirm that VSD II trapping remodels the activation and inactivation gating, whereas ECL III engagement contributes both to inhibition and activation. Subtype-specific sequence variations in the ECL III region underlie the prominent species- and…

items.title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates
items.summary_raw: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client–scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client–scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client–scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue–resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach…

items.title: Domain-encoded DNA barcodes for combinatorial multiplexed protein imaging via stepwise displacement
items.summary_raw: Multiplexed protein imaging via DNA barcoding faces a fundamental scaling constraint: Each target requires a distinct DNA identity, making barcode capacity grow only linearly with the number of validated sequences. Combinatorial encoding in RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization achieves exponential scaling by distributing shared readout sequences across dozens of probes per transcript, but antibody-based protein labeling lacks this multiprobe architecture. Here, we report domain-encoded DNA barcodes (DEDBs), which embed combinatorial identity within the internal domain organization of a single-stranded DNA scaffold. Three orthogonal encoding units arranged across three encoding domains define a theoretical design space of 27 barcodes. Sequence reuse does not compromise readout specificity: Each read strand spans two adjacent domains, so a mismatched read strand inevitably contains a continuous stretch of noncomplementary bases and forms a thermodynamically disfavored intermediate that is subsequently displaced by the perfectly matched strand. We term this self-correcting behavior thermodynamic proofreading, and a three-process kinetic model shows that specificity arises not from initial binding discrimination but from cognate-driven correction at the product level. Coupled with signal-amplified antibody labeling, DEDBs enable quantitatively decoded nine-target intracellular protein imaging in fixed cells. The same barcode library supports Polychrome trajectory decoding for…

items.title: Multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived biomimetic vesicles for cancer multimodal targeting and immune reprogramming
items.summary_raw: Despite advances of biomimetic vesicles in cancer therapy, clinical challenges such as biosafety, scalability, and therapeutic efficacy remain significant hurdles. To address these limitations, we reveal the critical tumor-homing motifs of cancer cell membrane vesicles: a synergistic “chemotactic recruitment-adhesion anchoring” cascade effect, especially chemokine axes (e.g., CXCL12/CXCR4) and integrins (e.g., αVβ3). In this study, we identify autologous fibroblasts as an ideal “chassis” cell for engineering biomimetic carriers. Using this platform, we construct multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived nanovesicles (X-Fb-MNVs) coexpressing critical chemokine receptor CXCR4 and adhesion ligand iRGD, as well as PD-1 and CD47 protein, which achieved robust and broad-spectrum tumor targeting across breast, liver, pancreatic, and colon cancer PDX models. Significantly, CD47-modified X-Fb-MNVs reduced hepatic accumulation and phagocytic clearance, thereby minimizing off-target effects in vivo and improving tumor targeting efficiency. By loading diABZI STING agonist into X-Fb-MNVs with overexpressed PD-1, our system activates both T cell and innate immunity, reversing ICB resistance and achieving 83.3% survival with no tumor recurrence and long-term immune surveillance over 90 d, whereas no mice survived with free diABZI treatment. By merging multimodal targeting, immune reprogramming, and scalable production into a single platform, X-Fb-MNVs represent a remarkable biomimetic system…

items.title: Nutritional niches reveal mutualism resilience in urban fungus-farming ants
items.summary_raw: Maintaining optimized nutrient exchange between partnered species across changing environments presents a fundamental challenge for nutritional mutualisms. Yet quantitative approaches linking nutrient acquisition by one partner with the nutritional requirements of the other have been lacking. Here we extend the Nutritional Geometry Framework from organisms and colonies to interspecific mutualisms by linking realized nutritional niches (RNNs) with nutritional performance landscapes to quantify nutritional homeostasis between interacting species. Nutritional analyses of thousands of DNA-barcoded plant fragments collected by free-ranging Panamanian leafcutter ants revealed that RNNs for fungal cultivar provisioning diverged between degraded urban and intact rainforest habitats. Despite this, colonies converged on similar nutritional intake targets that were similarly positioned relative to regions of high fungal performance, while fungal nutritional yield remained stable across habitats. These findings demonstrate that correspondence between colony nutritional intake and fungal nutritional performance provides a quantitative means of assessing nutritional homeostasis across interacting species and establishes a foundation for comparative analyses of nutrient exchange across mutualisms experiencing environmental change.

items.title: A circuit mechanism for psychosis vulnerability during perimenopause
items.summary_raw: The transition to menopause is a period of profound physiological change that encompasses nearly one-third of a woman’s lifespan and is associated with a distinct rise in the incidence of psychosis. Despite the clinical burden of menopause-associated psychosis, the circuit-level mechanisms linking reproductive aging to psychiatric vulnerability remain poorly defined. Current understanding is limited by rodent models that utilize abrupt surgical hormone loss, which fail to capture the progressive endocrine fluctuations and follicular depletion characteristic of the natural menopausal transition. Here, we investigate how the gradual transition from perimenopause to postmenopause regulates the ventral hippocampus-mesolimbic dopamine circuit, a pathway centrally implicated in the development of psychotic symptoms. Specifically, we show that the perimenopausal transition induces a transient state of ventral hippocampal hyperactivity that selectively drives dopamine system dysfunction, whereas this modulatory control is absent in the postmenopausal state. These findings reveal that psychosis-related circuit instability is precipitated specifically by the hormonal transition itself, rather than the persistent state of estrogen deficiency that follows. This contrasts with the long-standing “estrogen protection hypothesis,” which posits that low hormone levels are the primary driver of symptoms and explains why standard hormone replacement and antipsychotic therapies often yield…

items.title: Diffusive and advective transport in structurally anisotropic fibrous hydrogels
items.summary_raw: Changes in fiber orientation in structurally anisotropic fibrous extracellular matrices govern transport, distribution, and accumulation of biologically active molecules and therapeutic nanoparticles in tissues. Fundamental studies of advection-driven transport in such matrices are challenging because changes in network anisotropy are generally coupled with variation in fiber dimensions, density, and surface chemistry. Here, a fibrous hydrogel was engineered in which the type and degree of fiber orientation were decoupled from these structural characteristics. Advection of charge-neutral nanoparticle probes under physiologically relevant pressure gradients was studied in a channel geometry that imposed spatially nonuniform flow across the fibrous network. The probe advection was quantified by the time of probe permeation through the gel along the fastest flow path and the time of probe distribution within the gel. We show that the permeation timescale was governed by advection along the pressure gradient, whereas the distribution timescale transitioned between advection- and diffusion-limited behavior depending on fiber orientation and probe dimension. The decoupling between these timescales became more pronounced with stronger alignment along the pressure gradient and with increasing probe dimension. Scaling analysis and a fluid dynamics simulation model further provided mechanistic insight into these experimental findings. Together, these results identify the key…

items.title: Evolution, information content, and optimality of gene regulatory architectures
items.summary_raw: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype–phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive a maximization principle, which implies that genotype–phenotype maps will evolve to associate fit phenotypes with larger numbers of possible genotypes. Mathematically, this builds on analogies between population genetics and statistical physics, as well as optimal coding in information theory. The results are particularly interesting in the context of transcriptional regulation, where optimal values of certain parameters that determine the gene regulatory architecture can be derived even without a complete knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved. We illustrate the theory using a simplified model of transcription factor (TF) binding to cis-regulatory elements (CREs): the fraction of possible CREs across the entire genotype space that bind a given TF evolves to match the fraction of CREs under selection to bind that TF. Similar “frequency matching” results are expected to emerge generically, because selection implicitly moves the entire regulatory architecture toward a fitness maximum, determining the “replicated genotype–phenotype map” for all CREs, while it simultaneously adapts toward individually fit CREs on that map. We discuss the subtleties and limitations of the theory related to biophysical constraints and the need for…

items.title: SCN1B intron 3 retention results in a nonsense-mediated decay–sensitive mRNA linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
items.summary_raw: Biallelic variants in the voltage-gated sodium channel (VGSC) gene SCN1B are linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy type 52 (DEE52). SCN1B encodes two isoforms: transmembrane β1, generated by all 6 coding exons, and β1B, generated by exons 1 to 3 followed by retention of intron 3 ( SCN1B -IR). Transmembrane β1 subunits are multifunctional proteins that regulate sodium current and channel cell-surface expression, participate in cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion, and modulate transcription. Several DEE52 variants in the transmembrane β1 coding region have been shown to result in mixed loss-of-function. DEE52 variants are also identified in SCN1B -IR, yet their functional impacts remain unknown. Here, we provide evidence that SCN1B -IR is a cell type–specific, nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)–sensitive transcript. We investigate a severe biallelic DEE52 patient variant in intron 3, SCN1B c.449-2A>G, which results in expression of SCN1B -IR, but not transmembrane β1 transcripts. A transgenic mouse model that expresses SCN1B -IR, but not transmembrane β1, transcript phenocopies Scn1b null mice with seizures and early death. Thus, SCN1B -IR functions as an NMD-sensitive transcript that cannot compensate for the loss of transmembrane β1. We propose that future work may reveal SCN1B -IR to be a therapeutic target similar to other NMD-targeted transcripts.

items.title: Bouton-specific diversity of glutamate release from single parallel fiber axons in the cerebellum
items.summary_raw: Sensorimotor processing relies on high-frequency signaling across widespread neuronal networks, during which synapses undergo rapid short-term plasticity (STP) that transiently enhances or depresses synaptic strength. Although STP is known to vary across cell types and postsynaptic targets, it remains unclear whether and how it is regulated at the level of individual synaptic boutons along the same axon. Here, we used two-photon imaging of a fast genetically encoded glutamate sensor expressed in cerebellar granule cells to monitor glutamate release from individual parallel fiber boutons during trains of activity. We showed that along single axons, glutamate transients were detected at nearly all boutons, and displayed a high diversity of STP profiles. At individual boutons, initial synaptic weight and STP were regulated separately. Synaptic weight was primarily driven by release probability ( P r ) and the apparent number of functional release sites ( N ), whereas STP was mainly supported by rapid mobilization of synaptic vesicles. At the molecular level, we show that Synapsin II contributes to bouton-specific heterogeneity in release properties. These findings reveal that STP is regulated at the level of individual boutons by specific molecular determinants, enabling fine-tuned control of information flow in cerebellar circuits. A single granule cell could therefore translate an identical presynaptic spike pattern into distinct release dynamics at each of its boutons, thus…

items.title: There Are Suddenly a Lot of Climate Movies
items.summary_raw: I am, I confess, a bit of a climate media skeptic . The literary sub-genre of “cli-fi” has become so bogged down by tropes that even the judges of a prize for the best climate fiction of the year made reading the contenders sound like a slog . (“So many small groups of humans roaming a post-apocalyptic landscape,” bemoaned one adjacent novelist.) On TV, climate protagonists frequently serve as mouthpieces for big ideas , backgrounded by cartoonishly greedy capitalists and bad CGI. At least watching a disaster movie, you get to enjoy the spectacle of a firenado taking out the Golden Gate Bridge before sitting through a moralizing speech at the end about “coming together” and “protecting the planet.” My skepticism about Hollywood’s penchant for turning liberal consensus causes into “important,” “urgent,” and narratively and artistically hollow products is part of why I still haven’t seen the marquee climate movie of the year, Digger. (Having a 13-month-old is, admittedly, the other part). But there is no denying that climate movies are having a moment: Spotlight director Tom McCarthy’s adaptation of Nathaniel Rich’s book Losing Earth , A Statement , is due out early next year, and premiered this fall at festivals to generally positive reviews (though a trio of adjectives from The Daily Beast suggests it hasn’t entirely escaped the pitfalls of the genre, with the outlet’s critic calling it “ preachy, humorless, and unenlightening ”). “Five years ago, I could not have imagined…

items.title: Ekonomika je na tom hůř než před rokem, vláda bude mít co obhajovat před svými voliči

items.summary_raw: If General Flash has it right, America may have a new way to refine nearly every critical metal it now buys from China. The Cambridge, Massachusetts-based startup emerged from stealth Tuesday with $128 million in combined seed and Series A funding from Lux Capital, Lowercarbon Capital, Overmatch Ventures, Construct Capital, and others. The MIT spinout is pioneering “new physics,” its founder and CEO, Ric Fulop, told me, which allows it to refine metal oxides into high-purity metals using an electrolytic process that produces no direct emissions. The company has already broken ground on its first commercial facility, a 1,000-metric-ton per year plant in Massachusetts that Fulop said will begin production next summer. If the technology delivers on its promise, it could greatly reduce U.S. dependence on China for metals such as tungsten, titanium, tantalum, zirconium, and rare earths — materials used throughout semiconductor, defense, aerospace and advanced manufacturing supply chains. Although many of these minerals are mined around the world, China controls more than 80% of global refining capacity for some of them. “Usually metals refining is not a very clean industry,” Fulop told me. “Maybe that’s one of the reasons that we looked the other way when China started taking a lot of market share in the space in the last 20 years.” General Flash’s process, which the company calls “solid-state flash electrolysis,” works by subjecting heated metal oxide powders to intense…

How Tribes Became Power Players on Permitting Reform
items.summary_raw: One big sticking point that’s emerged in negotiations over the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act are the changes it would make to the National Historic Preservation Act. The bill would rewrite Section 106 of that law, which requires the federal government to consult with tribal nations before it permits a major project on or adjacent to land of Native cultural value. Crucially, the protections in Section 106 of the NHPA don’t end at the borders of a reservation. They extend to public and private property, as well. The initial version of the legislation would have shrunk the scope and shortened the deadlines of reviews under the NHPA, and imposed punitive new rules on the officials in charge of overseeing those processes. It would have also allowed the federal government to step in and take over a local official’s office if officials thought they weren’t moving quickly enough. A subsequent amendment would soften many of those revisions, but not all of them. Tribes have emerged as one of the most important players in the permitting bill negotiations. items.title: Tribes push back as Congress moves to fast-track energy projects
items.summary_raw: After years of negotiation, Congress is on the cusp of passing a bipartisan “permitting reform” bill that would make it far easier to build power plants and electric transmission lines in the United States. The bill was negotiated by a bipartisan group of senators including Democrat Sheldon Whitehouse, a noted climate hawk, and Republican Mike Lee, an opponent of environmental regulation. It has picked up support from clean energy advocates because it would promote more transmission lines to carry renewable power to cities, speed up review for solar and wind projects, and stop presidents from cancelling offshore wind farms. It has also been endorsed by many conservative , business , and fossil fuel groups, who say it would cut down on environmental red tape and speed up natural gas pipelines. The bill has divided the climate movement , separating groups focused on decarbonization from those focused on endangered species protection and environmental justice, but the most influential opposition has come from tribal nations. The bill would weaken a historic preservation law that tribes often use to protect cultural and religious sites from development, and numerous prominent Indigenous nations and organizations have said it harms tribal sovereignty. While the bill cleared a procedural hurdle in the Senate last week, it remains unclear whether it will pass there or in the House. items.title: Nitrates in drinking water are a ‘public health crisis,’ environmentalists warn
items.summary_raw: When the federal government set its limit on how much nitrate drinking water can safely contain, the primary concern was blue baby syndrome, a condition that deprives infants of oxygen. In the 51 years since then, research has associated exposure to the contaminant with cancer and other health problems, fueling calls for a stricter standard. On Monday, a coalition of national and local advocacy organizations including the Natural Resources Defense Council, Union of Concerned Scientists, Prairie Rivers Network, and 11 others filed a petition calling on the U.S Environmental Protection Agency to lower that threshold from 10 milligrams per liter to 1 mg/liter. In its petition, the coalition argued that “nitrates in drinking water are causing a public health crisis across the country.” “One in three Americans — nearly 120 million people in this country — are currently being served water with dangerous levels of nitrate in it,” said Tyler Lobdell, a senior staff attorney at Food & Water Watch. That figure includes people served water with nitrate concentrations above 1 mg/L — one-tenth of the current federal standard. Nitrate pollution, much of it linked to fertilizer and manure runoff and leaching from agriculture, is a particular concern in farming regions, where contaminated groundwater can disproportionately impact rural, low-income, Latino , and farmworker communities. Studies have linked exposure with colorectal cancer, thyroid disease, and fetal abnormalities. A 2019 study…

That’s because, as retail investors are now discovering, Huang was more than just a tech CEO — he was a “one-person coordination function.” Under Huang, Nvidia was a generous financier of what often gets called the broader AI “ecosystem.” Nvidia didn’t just design the chips that made the world go round. It lent money to the companies buying the chips, backed data center projects housing them, and invested in software companies that planned to use the data centers. That money machine has been enormously profitable, propelling Nvidia to a more than $5 trillion market cap at its peak. But it may also be prone to jolts and sudden stops. If Nvidia’s new interim CEO, Colette Kress, or her permanent replacement are less risk-prone than Huang, then it could reshape the entire AI sector. items.title: Personal troubles and public issues: Bringing everyday talk into energy research and policy
items.summary_raw: This paper introduces everyday talk as an important agenda for energy research and policymaking. Connecting with recent research on social relations and energy communication, we show that everyday conversations about energy are important sites of social learning and decision-making. We first discuss the understated importance of talk to three leading approaches within energy social science: environmental psychology; practice theory; and relational sociology. Subsequently, we develop a ‘talk-in-interaction’ approach based on ethnomethodology and conversation analysis (EMCA) to examine everyday energy conversations and ‘word of mouth’ effects within two rural communities in Scotland. Our analysis investigates the sociological effects of energy silences, storytelling, and conversational learning on wider processes of energy transition and technology uptake. We conclude by identifying future trajectories for a new research programme investigating energy talk and opportunities for energy policy to better engage community members' everyday concerns regarding energy. Policymakers must empower devolved, locally-embedded energy support to enable policy that is responsive to community members' changing needs and escape the reductive and polarising communication of formal consultation.

items.title: Sea level rise in Los Santos and Los Angeles: a comparative flood analysis using Grand Theft Auto V
items.summary_raw: We present the first quantitative GIS-based flood inundation analysis using terrain data reproduced from a commercial video game, applied to the fictional city of Los Santos from Grand Theft Auto V (GTA V) under two contrasting IPCC Fifth Assessment Report (AR5) Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios (RCP 2.6, strong mitigation, and RCP 8.5, high-emission baseline) combined with historical storm surge records from the Los Angeles tide gauge, across three time horizons (2100, 2300, and 2500). Los Santos serves as an ideal case study because it faithfully replicates Los Angeles (LA), enabling direct comparison of simulated flood outcomes in the game world with published scientific vulnerability analyses for LA. Results indicate that Los Santos is modelled with sufficient geomorphological detail for projected flooding patterns to closely resemble those identified for Los Angeles, including the spatial sequence of inundation across the marina district, the Pacific Palisades coastline, and the port. Under the RCP 8.5 scenario with storm surges, combined sea levels are projected to reach 5.18 m by 2300, with the model showing 5.1 % of the mapped land area inundated; for a 2500 scenario with projected sea levels of 8.22 m this increases to 6.5 % modelled inundation, which places the port, wastewater infrastructure, and coastal energy facilities at risk. Under the RCP 2.6 mitigation scenario the model shows 2.2 % of land area inundated at 2300 with storm surge, with no…

items.title: Whose priorities? Media reporting and the output legitimacy of International Organizations
items.summary_raw: Traditional accounts of output legitimacy emphasize that support for multipurpose international organizations (IOs) depends on their ability to deliver effective policies. We argue that legitimacy beliefs also hinge on which policies IOs are perceived to prioritize, and that media reporting on the policy focus of international organizations plays an important role in this process. Such reporting can shape legitimacy beliefs by influencing the extent to which citizens perceive an IO’s policy output to align with their own ideological preferences. Using the European Union as a test case, we analyze over 400,000 news articles from Austria, France, Germany, and Spain with semi-supervised machine learning to identify issue emphasis. We link this to Eurobarometer survey data capturing individual-level assessments of the EU’s output legitimacy. We find that citizens tend to evaluate the EU more positively when media coverage highlights policy areas aligned with their ideology. These findings suggest that citizens judge IOs not only by how well they perform, but also by whose priorities they are perceived to serve.

items.title: Climate narratives and media coverage in different regimes
items.summary_raw: Different forms of government may exhibit different levels of environmental commitment. Previous studies indicate that democracies are often more likely than autocracies to adopt environmental protection policies. In this paper, we examine whether regime type is also associated with differences in media coverage of climate change. As political institutions can be associated with press freedom and the media environment, we aim to investigate whether democratic and non-democratic countries differ in the volume of climate change reporting. Through a quantitative econometric analysis, we explore the relationship between political institutions and climate-related newspaper articles published by a selection of monitored media outlets. The analysis, based on media and institutional data for 16 countries over the period 2004–2023, examines whether democracies exhibit higher levels of climate change media coverage compared to their autocratic counterparts, while accounting for selected economic and environmental factors. In particular, we also consider whether autocracies display substantial climate-related coverage, potentially consistent with more centralized communication strategies, or whether climate change receives comparatively limited media attention. The results indicate a positive association between democratic status and the normalized volume of climate change media coverage across the specifications considered. However, the limited variation in political regime type over…

items.title: ASSESSMENT OF ENERGY EFFICIENCY DESIGN STRATEGIES IN MIXED-USE BUILDINGS IN ABUJA
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT The demand for energy in mixed use buildings, high rate of urbanisation and environmental issues have heightened the need for energy-efficient building design. This study investigated the integration of energy-efficient design strategies in the design of a mixed-use building in Abuja with a view to optimising energy performance of buildings and to improve the comfort and well-being of the occupants. The study employed both qualitative and quantitative methods to provide a robust assessment of energy efficiency strategies in mixed-use buildings. The quantitative approach was adopted using structured questionnaires administered to 168 registered architects and 90 occupants of selected mixed-use buildings in Abuja. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, while case studies of the World Trade Centre Abuja, Nestoil Tower Lagos, Kingway Tower Lagos, and Nurol Tower provided extensive knowledge of existing passive strategies. The findings showed that natural ventilation systems (Mean = 3.95), atria, courtyards and sky gardens (Mean = 3.60), mixed mode ventilation (Mean = 3.54), energy efficient lighting systems (Mean = 3.53), and daylight harvesting strategies (Mean = 3.52) were the most integrated strategies. These measures were found to improve energy performance by reducing operational energy consumption, lowering peak energy demand, enhancing thermal comfort, improving indoor air quality, and promoting occupants' well-being. However, high cost of materials…

items.title: Broadcast Media and Climate Change Communication in Nigeria: Evidence from Taraba State
items.source_name: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
items.summary_raw: This study examined broadcast media and climate change communication in Taraba State, Nigeria. It assessed residents’ climate change knowledge, exposure to radio and television information, the relationship between perceived message effectiveness and adaptive actions, and barriers to effective communication. Agenda Setting Theory and Knowledge, Attitude, Behaviour (KAB) model were adopted as theoretical framework. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. The study covered three Local Government Areas purposively selected from the Northern, Central, and Southern senatorial zones: Jalingo, Bali, and Takum. The 2006 National Population Commission figures for the three LGAs were projected to 2026 at a 3.1% annual growth rate, giving a total population of 894,821. A sample of 384 was determined using the Raosoft sample size calculator at a 95% confidence level and 5% margin of error. Multi-stage sampling was used: five wards were randomly selected from each LGA, and questionnaires were administered to eligible adult that were accessible and agreed to participate in the survey. Of the 384 questionnaires distributed, 366 were retrieved, representing a 95.3% response rate. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and Spearman’s rank-order correlation in SPSS version 25 at the 0.05 significance level. Findings showed moderate climate change knowledge, with correct responses on individual items ranging between 47.3% and 50.5%. Radio exposure was higher than…

items.title: From paradigms to instruments: ideational constraints on industrial policy and the Dutch National Growth Fund
items.summary_raw: The resurgence of industrial policy has sparked debate over whether contemporary state intervention marks a break with neoliberalism or rather its reconfiguration. We add nuance by shifting the focus from macro-level paradigms to meso-level instruments, developing an analytical framework for mapping industrial policy instruments based on two key dimensions: selectivity, the degree to which the state directs investment toward specific sectors, and conditionality, the discipline attached to public support. Neoliberal settings, such as those prevalent in high-income economies, encompass competing ideational currents with different views on these dimensions: Pro-business neoliberals favor selectivity to support competitive firms while placing less emphasis on conditionality, whereas frugal neoliberals prioritize conditionality to discipline public spending but are skeptical about selectivity. Instrument design reflects the negotiation between these competing currents. We illustrate this argument through a case study of the Dutch National Growth Fund, based on 24 semi-structured interviews and documentary analysis. We find that the dominance of frugal neoliberal ideas produced an instrument shaped more by conditionality than selectivity, suggesting that recent industrial policy initiatives have been bounded by intra-neoliberal contestation. The article contributes a meso-level analytical framework for analyzing variation in industrial policy design across high-income economies.

items.title: Regional governance of the energy transition: A comparison of spatial policies in Germany
items.summary_raw: The energy transition is a multifaceted and spatially differentiated transformation process that requires effective governance across multiple policy levels. While national and local energy governance has been widely examined, the regional level remains comparatively understudied despite its crucial role in translating strategic objectives into local implementation and in mediating between policy scales. This paper examines how regional energy transition governance in Germany is shaped through planning and policy instruments in different spatial contexts. This study undertakes a comparative policy screening of 199 formal and informal planning documents related to renewable energy development in three contrasting regions: the Ruhr Area, Western Pomerania, and the Upper Rhine. The analysis focuses on steering modes, degrees of formalisation, style of communication, and patterns of actor involvement to identify region-specific governance constellations. The results reveal clearly distinguishable regional governance profiles. The Ruhr Area is characterised by strategy-oriented governance coordinated predominantly through informal instruments with limited legal binding. Western Pomerania uses a more hierarchical and legally formalised approach, in which the public is addressed comparatively less frequently. The Upper Rhine exhibits a more cooperative and stakeholder-oriented governance profile, with municipalities, civil society, and scientific actors being relatively strongly…

items.title: Dynamic Socio‐Technical Simulation of CCU Adoption Under Uncertainty: Integrating Multi‐Criteria Decision Analysis and Agent‐Based Modeling
items.summary_raw: The large‐scale deployment of carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technologies requires decision‐making under technological uncertainty, evolving policy environments, economic constraints, and societal influence. Conventional techno‐economic and multi‐criteria assessments provide valuable insights but do not, by themselves, represent the dynamic interactions among facility adoption, regulatory responses, community conditions, and technological learning. This study develops an integrated socio‐technical simulation framework combining multi‐criteria decision analysis with agent‐based modeling and simulation to explore CCU adoption under alternative sustainability‐oriented decision priorities. The framework represents heterogeneous industrial facilities, nine sustainability‐related evaluation criteria, and feedback mechanisms involving regulatory incentives, social acceptance, and technology maturity. Five decision‐priority scenarios—climate, economy, energy, social, and infrastructure—are compared over a 30‐step simulation horizon. The results show substantial differences in adoption and system‐level performance. The climate scenario achieves the highest deployment, with 22 adopted facilities, and the greatest cumulative net avoidance (38 981.4 t) but also the highest cumulative hydrogen consumption and operating costs. Other scenarios exhibit different combinations of deployment, mitigation, and expenditure, indicating that no single scenario performs best across all…

items.title: Public opinion surveys with large language models: methodological opportunities and validity risks
items.summary_raw: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being considered as tools for computational social science, yet their implications for survey and public-opinion research remain insufficiently understood. This study examines whether and how they can serve as methodological instruments for estimating aggregate public opinion under out-of-sample conditions. Across three studies, commercial and open-source LLMs are evaluated against recent Pew Research Centre surveys. Study 1 shows that GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 can approximate national-level response distributions more accurately than uniform, normal-distribution, and historical-average baselines, with GPT-4 achieving mean absolute errors of approximately 4–8.5%. However, the models also exhibit important threats to validity, including underrepresentation of Republican viewpoints, underestimation of uncertainty, and, in some cases, overly homogeneous response distributions. Study 2 extends the analysis to GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Llama 3.3, showing that aggregate predictive accuracy generalises across models but that partisan alignment and distributional fidelity are model- and topic-dependent. Study 3 demonstrates that collective-level estimation is more valid than aggregating persona-based individual simulations, which produce substantially higher error and stronger homogeneity bias. Ablation tests further indicate that predictions are relatively robust to role prompts and temperature settings but sensitive to survey-item context…

items.title: Geographies of green sacrifice: Territorial inequalities in Spain's energy transition
Owning the wind, losing the voice? Community wind, equity & participation in Northern Germany
items.summary_raw: Community energy is widely presented as a pathway to democratic decarbonization, yet its inclusiveness remains uncertain. This study examines community wind in Dithmarschen, northern Germany, where citizen investment in wind has long been practiced. Building on an earlier, unpublished university survey of renewable energy communities, we retain its explanatory logic and survey instrument while centering a cross-sectional member survey of two community wind parks and situating all commensurable variables against consolidated German evidence. The analysis links observed participation patterns to concrete features of finance, governance, and recruitment. The results indicate that entry is shaped by household finance considerations and by the design of participation products. Required equity exposure, perceived risk, and product complexity select a narrower sociological base, while recruitment that moves through local networks limits the circle of potential entrants. Inside the organizations, formal authority is concentrated in managing entities, and member rights are primarily informational; unless routine reporting, agenda-linked consultation, and inclusive advisory formats are instituted, procedural and recognitional justice remain thin. At the same time, motives combine financial return with environmental and place-based identification, so that participation carries both private and civic meaning for those who enter. Conceptually, the case indicates that inclusiveness…

items.title: Where Climate Change Lands: Spatial Framing and Domestication in South Korean Newspapers, 2000–2025
items.summary_raw: This study analyzes 26 years of climate change coverage (2000–2025) across four major South Korean newspapers (n = 27,646) to examine how geographic framing varies across sub-national regions and shifts over time. Drawing on Olausson’s (2014, The diversified nature of “domesticated” news discourse: The case of climate change in national news media. Journalism Studies, 15(6), 711–725, https://doi.org/10.1080/1461670X.2013.837253) domestication typology and LLM-assisted classification, the analysis finds that extroverted domestication dominates Korean climate reporting but is historically unstable. Different triggering events are associated with different domestication modes, with introverted domestication peaking in 2010–2014, coinciding with the Low Carbon Green Growth policy period, and with climate disasters coinciding with a sharp introverted surge. Regional analysis of twelve sub-national locations reveals a structural asymmetry between metropolitan areas, imagined as sites of climate governance, and provincial regions, imagined as sites of climate consequence. These findings extend the domestication framework from the global-national to the national-sub-national scale and support a theoretical link between domestication and the production of place-based climate imaginaries.

items.title: Analysis of the impact and ambition of the new NDCs for 2035: Paris climate goal is further out of reach
items.summary_raw: In 2025, almost 130 countries submitted new national climate plans, known as nationally determined contributions (NDCs), outlining mitigation targets for 2035. This study evaluates their impact on emissions for all countries and assesses their ambition levels, with a main focus on the G20 economies. Full implementation of unconditional and conditional NDCs would reduce projected median global greenhouse gas emissions in 2035 by approximately 7% and 11% respectively, compared to 2019 levels—still falling short of the reductions needed to align with below 2°C and 1.5°C pathways. Among the G20, four economies—Australia, the EU, Japan, and the United Kingdom—have set new NDC targets on a linear path to net-zero emissions. In contrast, Brazil, Canada, the Russian Federation, and South Africa have NDCs misaligned with their net-zero targets. For the remaining G20 economies that have yet to peak—China, Indonesia, Mexico, the Republic of Korea, and Türkiye—transitioning to net-zero emissions must occur within 15 to 35 years, a timeline significantly shorter than the 37 to over 60 years required by those that have already peaked, underscoring the urgency for rapid decarbonization after 2035. Lastly, the majority of G20 economies do not meet 2035 reduction targets derived from Paris-aligned equity-based effort-sharing approaches.

items.title: Quality, reliability, and framing of EAT–lancet diet information on YouTube: a social media content analysis
items.summary_raw: Background The EAT–Lancet diet is a prominent framework for promoting healthy and sustainable diets within planetary boundaries. However, YouTube videos may present this complex model with varying levels of accuracy, completeness, and reliability. This study assessed the quality, reliability, source, message characteristics, video format, and stance of YouTube videos on the EAT–Lancet diet. Methods In this cross-sectional social media content analysis, YouTube was searched on May 1, 2026, using four EAT–Lancet-related keywords. After excluding duplicates, non-English videos, re-uploaded videos, and irrelevant content, 67 videos were analyzed. Video characteristics and engagement metrics were recorded, while speaker type, information source, message type, and stance were independently coded by the author and two independent coders (three raters in total). The same three raters assessed the videos using the DISCERN instrument. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Fisher’s exact test with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate adjustment, Cramer’s V, and Spearman correlations. Results Overall, 59.7% of videos were classified as medium quality, 19.4% as high quality, and 20.9% as low quality. Only 9.0% had high reliability. Nearly half of the videos were produced or shared by individual users. In exploratory format comparisons, standard videos were more frequently categorized as higher quality than Shorts; however, only 11 Shorts were available. Video length was…

items.title: Islamic Social Finance for Inclusive Green Finance: Pathways for Underbanked Farmers in Nigeria
items.source_name: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
items.summary_raw: Climate vulnerability and financial exclusion reinforce one another in Nigeria, where underbanked smallholder farmers face increasing exposure to droughts, floods, and other climate-related risks while experiencing limited access to affordable climate finance. Conventional green-finance mechanisms often require collateral, formal credit histories, and business documentation, creating significant barriers for vulnerable agricultural communities. This study examines how Islamic social finance can advance inclusive green finance for underbanked smallholder farmers in Nigeria. Using a qualitative deductive content analysis of academic literature, policy documents, and relevant case evidence, the study analyses the roles of Islamic microfinance, zakat, waqf, infaq, and qard hasan in supporting climate adaptation and sustainable agricultural development. The findings indicate that these instruments can provide Shariah-compliant, lower-cost, and more accessible financing for climate-smart agriculture, renewable-energy adoption, efficient irrigation, drought-resistant inputs, and small-scale green enterprise. Zakat can provide targeted assistance and interest-free financial support to eligible vulnerable farmers, while waqf can mobilise long-term capital for productive agricultural assets and shared green infrastructure. Infaq can support emergency relief and non-repayable resilience-building activities, while qard hasan provides interest-free financing for sustainable agricultural…

items.title: A Critical Investigation of Hydrogen-Based Decarbonization Pathways for Africa’s Heavy Industries
items.source_name: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
items.summary_raw: This paper examines the hydrogen potential as a means of decarbonization for heavy industries in Africa as a continent, focusing on its crucial role as an alternative to fossil fuels across several industries. It also evaluates hydrogen and its paramount role in the world decarbonization agenda with a focus on the economic and environmental effects. More specifically, hydrogen production pathways from renewable energy, for example, solar and wind energy, highlighting its gain in reducing carbon emissions and supporting a sustainable energy future. Furthermore, it evaluates the techno-economic assessment of the hydrogen production pathway in Africa. The review also highlights institutional, economic, and technical barriers and the essential infrastructure for the production and storage of hydrogen, specifically in the area of accomplishing the agenda for global energy transition. In addition, the study also emphasizes the importance of governmental policies and financial considerations as drivers of adoption of hydrogen technologies. The study concludes by outlining the future outlook and strategic recommendations for the transformative potential of hydrogen in decarbonizing key sectors, for example, the chemical industry, long-distance transportation, and heavy industry, such as the cement and steel industries. It depicts a remarkable contribution of hydrogen to a low-carbon global energy system and provides valuable insights into the role of hydrogen as a decarbonization…

items.title: A narrative policy framework approach to measure blame and credit strategies during the Swiss–EU negotiations
items.summary_raw: This article examines how policy actors use narrative strategies to claim credit, attribute blame, and deflect responsibility. Building on the blame avoidance literature, it integrates the Narrative Policy Framework (NPF) to conceptualize presentational strategies as combinations of narrative causal mechanisms and devil–angel–solidarity shifts. Empirically, the study analyzes press releases by the Swiss government and the two major political parties during the Swiss–EU negotiations (2013–2025). The findings show that narrative strategies systematically align with credit and blame strategies: credit claiming and attribution are predominantly associated with intentional causal narratives and angel shifts, whereas blame attribution is linked to intentional causal mechanisms and devil shifts. Governmental actors primarily engage in credit claiming, while political parties focus on blame attribution. Credit claiming remains the predominant strategy of the government, even under declining policy support. The study contributes to the public policy literature by linking blame avoidance and NPF research, offering a novel measurement approach, and refining expectations about governmental communication under political contestation.

items.title: Potentials for Sustainable Irrigation in Humid Climate Zones: Building a Case for Sierra Leone's Climate and Ecologies
items.summary_raw: Irrigation is conventionally framed as an arid-land technology, yet the fastest relative growth in irrigated area now occurs in humid and sub-humid regions, where rainfall is abundant in total but poorly distributed within the year. This review examined the physical, agronomic, and institutional potentials for sustainable irrigation in humid climate zones and applied the resulting framework to Sierra Leone, a country receiving 1,900–4,000 mm of rainfall annually yet growing a single rain-fed crop on most of its farmland. Published hydrological assessments, global irrigation-expansion modelling, humid-region field trials, and national land and water statistics were synthesised. Sierra Leone holds internal renewable water resources of about 160 km³ yr⁻¹ against agricultural withdrawals of roughly 0.33 km³ yr⁻¹, under 0.3% of the resource, while only about 1,000 ha of a technically assessed 807,000 ha potential had been equipped. The binding constraint was therefore temporal and infrastructural rather than volumetric: the December–March dry season delivers only 6–7% of annual rainfall against open-water evaporation of 1,200–1,900 mm yr⁻¹, producing a seasonal deficit that idles 1.165 million ha of lowlands, of which inland valley swamps account for about 690,000 ha. Global modelling indicated that soft-path irrigation using small monthly storage, combined with 20% deficit irrigation, could sustainably expand irrigation over about 8 million ha in sub-Saharan Africa without…

items.title: Hazard hexagons: the influence of anthropogenic climate change on extremes in regions globally
items.summary_raw: The sixth assessment report (AR6) of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change presented regional summaries of the scientific knowledge of changing weather extremes and the human influence upon this. The hexagon figures, found in the summary for policymakers, were a key part of this presentation. They provided clear visual overviews of this understanding on three hazard types (hot extremes, heavy precipitation and agricultural and ecological drought) for policymakers, scientists and communicators alike. We have shown that since 2021, when AR6 was published, there has been a rapid advancement in knowledge of changing extremes on the timescale of individual years, with a greater than doubling in the number of extreme event and trend attribution studies coupled with advances in methodologies, rising levels of anthropogenic forcing, and a growing sample of manifested extreme events. The coming seventh assessment report (AR7) is an opportunity to update and iterate these figures, expand to other hazard types and, we argue, to facilitate more regular updates in line with this rapidly advancing field of knowledge. To this end, we have updated the AR6 hexagons in several ways: we have added evidence levels to the figures to provide additional information without sacrificing visual clarity; we have built on the AR6 regional synthesis process with a step-by-step procedure and accompanying expert guidance and discussion; we have applied this to six illustrative regional case…

items.title: The Importance of Remedies in Climate Litigation: Illustrations in English Private Law
items.summary_raw: Existing scholarship in climate litigation focuses predominantly on the substantive aspects of the cases, examining the compatibility of legal frameworks with climate goals, judicial attitudes, and doctrinal constraints. While valuable, most neglect a crucial dimension: the remedial aspects of climate litigation. Remedies are not merely technical afterthoughts that follow successful claims; they are deeply entangled with the substantive law, and the viability of the remedy can have a material impact on litigation outcomes. This article explores this issue in the context of private law. Foregrounding remedies, it analyses recent private law litigation in the English courts, questioning the feasibility of certain litigation strategies and offering insights for strategic improvements. This focus is timely given the recent prioritization of private law strategies in global climate litigation, including in England.

items.title: The Role of Banking Development and Renewable Energy in Shaping Environmental Sustainability in Saudi Arabia: Evidence from a Bootstrap ARDL Approach
items.source_name: Journal of Administrative and Economic Sciences
items.summary_raw: Objectives Environmental sustainability remains a central policy concern for economies undergoing structural diversification, particularly in carbon-intensive nations such as Saudi Arabia, yet the influence of banking-sector development remains comparatively under-examined. This study investigates how banking development, renewable energy consumption, and economic growth shape environmental sustainability in Saudi Arabia using both carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and the load capacity factor (LCF). Material and Methods LCF provides a composite measure that integrates ecological footprint and bio-capacity, thereby enabling an assessment of environmental sustainability beyond conventional single-dimensional measures. Using an annual dataset covering 1980–2024, we estimate two environmental models employing the bootstrap autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) framework. Results Findings indicate long-run co-integration among the variables. Banking-sector development significantly reduces CO₂ emissions and enhances LCF in the long run, demonstrating the potential for green financial intermediation to support national sustainability goals. Renewable energy consumption consistently improves environmental indicators, while economic growth displays an inverted U-shaped association with both CO₂ and LCF, supporting the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC). CUSUM and CUSUMSQ tests confirm parameter stability. Conclusion The study concludes with policy implications aligned with Saudi…
