items.title: Coupled human–cattle mobility shaped the socioeconomic landscapes of the Holocene Middle Nile Valley
items.summary_raw: We present a synthesis of strontium isotope data ( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) from human and cattle dental enamel across Middle Nile. This dataset, which combines newly acquired and published measurements, reveals a complex history of human and cattle mobility linked to ecological gradients and sociocultural changes in this part of the continent. During the early Holocene (8,000 to 4,000 BCE), isotopic unanimity in human and cattle remains supports early, correlated mobility of humans and Bos , extending beyond Nile floodplains to adjacent uplands. In the mid-Holocene (4,000 to 1,000 BCE), isotopic data from Wadi Howar suggest bidirectional corridors for mobility of both species linking the Middle Nile and the Western Desert. This pattern correlates with the emergence of the Middle Nile civilizations in which cattle played a central cultural and economic role. From the first millennium BCE onward, a radical change can be observed, correlated with the progressive desertification processes in the Sahel. Although cattle import routes continued to follow wadi systems, they shifted south of the now desiccated Saharan lakes toward Kordofan. The long-term perspective emphasizes the continuous adaptation of societies in the Middle Nile of what is now Sudan and adjacent regions to environmental changes, aimed at maintaining sustained access to cattle, a resource that remained crucial for Middle Nile communities throughout the Holocene.

items.title: Vessel noise pollution offsets marine mammal energy budgets
items.summary_raw: Shipping is a major global source of underwater noise pollution and is frequently reported to alter the behavior of marine mammals. However, the energetic consequences of these noise-induced behavioral disruptions and their implications for population fitness remain poorly quantified. Using behavioral proxies of energy acquisition and expenditure derived from high-resolution sound and movement tags on 28 wild harbor porpoises, we estimate that porpoises decrease energy acquisition by 20% (range: 1 to 36%) during high-noise vessel exposures, while maintaining constant energy expenditure. With a median of 11 high-noise vessel exposures per day, these disruptions may result in an average daily shortfall of 4.6% of their net energy budget. Sustained over time, such noise-induced energetic deficits have the potential to compromise individual fitness, ultimately affecting the dynamics of harbor porpoise populations in industrialized coastal areas worldwide and reducing their functional carrying capacity. This framework establishes a direct mechanistic link between behavioral disruption and fitness-relevant impacts, providing a biologically grounded metric for predicting population-level outcomes of noise pollution and an objective basis for defining acceptable exposure levels of vessel noise for wild marine mammal populations. Moreover, it is scalable across species and ecosystems and offers a common currency for assessing the cumulative effects of multiple stressors in the…

items.title: Short-term flexibility and long-term stability in models of mind perception
items.summary_raw: Understanding how people decide whether someone or something possesses a mind is central to a myriad of psychological, biological, and philosophical questions. It shapes fundamental processes at the individual (e.g., social interaction) and societal level (e.g., morality and ethics). While mind perception has been studied, it remains unclear which internal model people use when ascribing mental capacities to entities. Across four experiments (total N = 256), we explored what model people hold and its flexibility when ascribing agency and experience to entities encountered in everyday life and which differ in animacy and socialness (e.g., humans, pets, robots, voice assistants, tools). Using representational similarity analysis combined with lab-based experiments, a 6-wk long social interaction intervention, and longitudinal real-life exposure, we tested which model people use to ascribe agency and experience by comparing observed rating data to theoretical models. We demonstrated that an animacy distinction underlies the representational structure of experience attributions, while internal models for agency attributions are more idiosyncratic and flexible. When receiving explicit information on one entity, the internal model of agency changes. People update their model by incorporating this information, generalizing across the entire category of entities. We found no evidence that extended exposure to or ownership of inanimate technology, such as robots or voice assistants…

items.title: isSPA-vesicle: AI-assisted structure determination of membrane proteins on vesicles
items.summary_raw: The demand for three-dimensional reconstruction of membrane proteins in native lipid environments has grown substantially in recent years. Both single-particle analysis and tomographic techniques have enabled structural studies across diverse vesicular samples; however, these methods remain limited in either efficiency or resolution. Here, we present an AI-enabled, vesicle geometry-guided 3D reconstruction strategy based on untilted data. Given that some vesicles exhibit anisotropic shapes in solution and adopt near-spherical or ellipsoidal geometries, we trained an AI model to estimate membrane geometric parameters and compute normal vectors based on the fitted ellipsoidal surface. This information facilitates post hoc filtering of particles picked using the isSPA framework based on the angular difference between their orientations and the membrane normals, and also enables the exclusion of particles outside the vesicles. This allows efficient localization of target membrane proteins enabling near-atomic-resolution reconstruction. Using this approach, we efficiently reconstructed membrane proteins ranging from 130 kDa to 2 MDa across two classes of enveloped viruses and three types of synthetic liposomes, achieving 2.7 Å resolution for influenza A virus hemagglutinin and 3.1 Å for the prefusion spike protein of HCoV-OC43. Our method provides a simple and efficient tool for achieving such reconstructions in physiological lipid bilayers.

items.title: The evolution and function of eukaryote-to-cyanobacteria horizontal gene transfer
items.summary_raw: Prokaryote-to-eukaryote horizontal gene transfer (HGT) has emerged as a driver of eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, eukaryote-to-prokaryote HGT remains poorly characterized, limiting insight into how eukaryote-derived genes influence prokaryotic evolution and function. Here, we reconstructed a comprehensive and well-resolved phylogeny of 469 high-quality Cyanobacteria genomes spanning all orders. Leveraging this framework, we identified 204 candidate functionally diverse genes of eukaryotic origin in cyanobacteria, likely representing 59 putative transfer events, including 197 genes not previously documented. All 204 candidates were intronless, consistent with intron loss during their evolutionary history. Transcriptomics reveal that HGT-acquired genes are expressed at significantly higher levels than both genome-wide and functionally matched non-HGT-acquired genes, suggesting functional importance. Notably, 138 genes exhibited functional annotations absent from the host cyanobacteria. We further characterized a granule-bound starch synthase (GBSS) putatively acquired by Crocosphaera from an ancestral archaeplastid lineage, enabling starch synthesis that may facilitate energy storage for nocturnal nitrogen fixation. These findings reveal that eukaryote-to-prokaryote gene transfer is an underappreciated driver of cyanobacterial evolution and function, with broad implications for microbial ecology, functional adaptation, and cross-domain genetic exchange.

items.title: Training of human spatial skills: Brain activity as a window to the mind’s eye
Correction for Adams et al., System-level synchronization and subtype-specific modules govern brain-wide serotonin axon innervation
Pollen tubes beat the heat
Transoceanic dispersals and island extinctions shape global snipe and woodcock diversity
items.summary_raw: Island colonization through transoceanic dispersal has been central in shaping insular biodiversity. Following colonization, island populations often undergo morphological shifts, which may promote ecological specialization and endemism, but often increase vulnerability to extinction. Most species in the shorebird family Scolopacidae are highly migratory, which likely underpins their propensity for long-distance dispersal. Notably, snipes ( Gallinago , Coenocorypha ) and woodcocks ( Scolopax ) have colonized diverse island regions, including the southwest Pacific, Malay Archipelago, Japan’s Amami, and the Caribbean, although none of the extant island endemics are migratory. The southwest Pacific and Caribbean taxa have suffered substantial recent extinction driven by human impacts. Here, we investigate avian evolutionary and biogeographic dynamics using a combination of morphology and phylogenomic data from target capture sequencing of key extant and extinct snipes and woodcocks. Our results reveal four independent dispersals from the Eastern to Western Hemisphere and a trans-Pacific dispersal from South America to the southwest Pacific islands. Comparative analyses of migratory behavior and morphology demonstrate pronounced changes in insular groups. For example, the small Austral snipes Coenocorypha are nested within Gallinago , sister to a group of much larger, continental South American snipes. Another case is the extinct Scolopax brachycarpa of Hispaniola which…

items.title: Stature reveals changing patterns of the biological standard of living in Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 y
items.summary_raw: Human stature is a valuable indicator of nutritional status and health. Reconstructing this indicator allows insights into which types of societies were providing better health and nutrition—also termed the “biological standard of living” in the literature. Yet, archaeological evidence has not previously been assembled on a scale large enough for systematic comparison across premodern Eurasia. We present a dataset of 18,457 stature observations based on 783 sites from Asia and Europe, roughly spanning the 7,000 y before the twentieth century. Using harmonized estimates derived from long bones, we document broad regional variation in stature over time and examine how these patterns relate to population density and historical indicators of technological development. We observe marked declines in stature in most regions during the 500–1900 CE period, in both Asia and Europe. To interpret these patterns, we combine our stature series with estimates of population density, technological advancement, and related controls. As [Q. Ashraf, O. Galor, Am. Econ. Rev. 101 , 2003–2041 (2011)] predicted, higher technology levels were associated with higher population density, but not correlated with higher stature before the modern era. This relationship also holds after controlling for other potentially confounding factors such as latitude or transport access. By assembling the largest archaeological stature dataset for Eurasia to date and linking it to long-term demographic and historical…

items.title: Localization mechanisms and function of postsynaptic K v 7 (KCNQ) channels and their reduction in KCNQ2 epileptic encephalopathy
items.summary_raw: K v 7 channels composed of K v 7.2 and K v 7.3 subunits are enriched in neuronal axons where their hyperpolarizing potassium current suppresses repetitive and burst firing of action potentials. Mutations in their genes, KCNQ2 and KCNQ3 , cause neonatal epilepsy, underscoring their critical role in regulating neuronal excitability. In this study, we provide evidence that K v 7 channels are present at and near the postsynaptic density within dendritic spines of hippocampal neurons, where their current decreases calcium influx through NMDA receptors. This spine localization is promoted by heteromerization of K v 7.2 and K v 7.3 and their binding to AnkyrinG-190, which is the only AnkyrinG isoform present in dendritic spines. Lastly, spine localization of K v 7 channels and their ability to suppress NMDA receptor activity are markedly reduced by select variants of KCNQ2 that cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). These findings reveal a subcellular population of K v 7 channels that can dampen excitatory synaptic transmission and implicate their dysregulation in KCNQ2 -associated DEE.

items.title: Impact pathways of a jurisdictional approach to slowing deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon
items.summary_raw: Governance of many of the world’s largest remaining tropical forests is shared across multiple levels of government, giving subnational jurisdictions a central role in forest management. This has motivated growing interest in jurisdictional approaches (JAs) to control deforestation. For JAs to deliver on national and international conservation priorities, those priorities must be translated into incentives that reduce deforestation at the jurisdictional level. Brazil’s Priority List (PL), launched in 2008, creates such incentives by identifying high-deforestation municipalities, subjecting them to intensified monitoring, enforcement, and credit restrictions, and establishing jurisdiction-wide criteria for exit that make municipalities accountable for deforestation within their borders. While prior studies show that the PL reduces deforestation, it remains unclear where these reductions occur and whether there is displacement across land tenure types or into neighboring municipalities. We assemble a municipality-level panel dataset for the Brazilian Legal Amazon (2000–2024) that combines PL designations with annual deforestation disaggregated by land tenure. Using a heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences estimator, we estimate effects within and across municipalities. We find large and statistically significant reductions concentrated on private lands, including agrarian reform settlements and other private properties. Within listed municipalities, we find no evidence…

items.title: Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 participates in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins
items.summary_raw: Microsatellite repeat expansion of the 5′ GGGGCC 3′ sequence in the C9orf72 gene is the most common monogenic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Dipeptide repeat proteins (DPRs) translated from the mutant allele can be detected in postmortem brains of afflicted individuals. The arginine containing peptides, poly proline-arginine (poly-PR) and poly glycine-arginine (poly-GR), are particularly noxious to cells. Both can undergo cell-to-cell transmission, but underlying mechanisms are not understood. We found rapid internalization and nucleolar localization of bath-applied hemagglutinin (HA) tagged poly-PR with twenty repeats (HA-PR 20 ) in cell lines and neurons. Small molecule and RNAi approaches implicated a temperature-dependent, fluid phase endocytosis mechanism for HA-PR 20 . We sought to identify DPR-related cell surface uptake factors using µMap high-resolution proximity labeling. DPR–iridium conjugates identified candidate cell-surface proteins which were interrogated in a secondary RNAi screen. Focusing on our strongest candidate, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4), we showed cellular uptake of HA-PR 20 is reduced by inhibition of glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis and knockdown or ablation of CSPG4. Knockdown of CSPG4 protected PR 20 -induced neuronal toxicity. Using a dual reporter system to interrogate in vitro neuron-to-neuron transmission of PR 50, we found PR 50 synthesized by one neuron readily spread to neighboring cells…

items.title: Correction for Davydova et al., Affect labeling down-regulates amygdala only in a dominant native language
The broad-spectrum RumC1 bacteriocin targets a transient peptidoglycan intermediate of the nascent cell wall
items.summary_raw: Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling, and single-cell fluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate that RumC1 is a distinct cell-wall-targeting toxin. First, all RumC1-resistant mutants isolated through a high-rate, genome-wide mutagenic screening exhibited specific impairments in peptidoglycan homeostasis regulation, pinpointing this pathway as critical for RumC1 activity. Second, RumC1 selectively accumulates within neosynthesized peptidoglycan, leading to cell growth arrest and death in a dose-dependent manner. Third, we characterize the RumI c 1 immunity protein of the RumC1 biosynthetic cluster as a peptidase acting at the cell surface to protect the cells by trimming the stem peptide crucial for cell-wall assembly. As such, RumI c 1 provides cross-protection against vancomycin, while RumC1 is demonstrated to act differently from this glycopeptide antibiotic. Collectively, these findings establish RumC1 as a toxin targeting a key peptidoglycan intermediate of cell wall maturation, which defines a distinct mode of action among the large and highly diverse repertoire of bacteriocins characterized so far.

items.title: The AI scientist in the mirror: Shared flaws, joint remedies
A decadal record of isotopic trends in martian atmospheric CO 2
items.summary_raw: This work represents the first long-term record of the isotopic composition of martian atmospheric CO 2 , acquired in situ by the Curiosity rover at Gale crater during Mars Years (MY) 31–38 (2012–2025). Measurement campaigns were designed to investigate possibilities of both diurnal and seasonal effects on CO 2 isotopes. Coordinated pairs of analyses during MY 31 and 38 revealed no significant differences in isotopic composition of CO 2 acquired during daytime and nighttime hours. However, here we show evidence for modest enrichment in heavy isotopes of oxygen in both northern and southern hemisphere spring-summer seasons. We assessed several processes, including precipitation/sublimation and adsorption/desorption of CO 2 , CO 2 photolysis, and oxygen isotope exchange as potential candidates for producing the observed fractionations. We find that while sublimation of CO 2 from polar caps, sublimation and desorption of CO 2 from lower latitude reservoirs, and CO 2 photolysis are insufficient alone, we can reproduce the measured enrichment through modeling of isotope exchange between CO 2 and 18 O-enriched H 2 O in thin liquid-like films at Mars’ surface or adsorbed within the regolith as Mars approaches and transits through perihelion. Lesser 18 O enrichment near aphelion may reflect less favorable conditions for oxygen isotope exchange at lower temperatures. Observed seasonal variations in CO 2 carbon isotopic composition are less pronounced, consistent with less carbon…

items.title: Leptin Receptor + cells create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis in the bone marrow by synthesizing CXCL14
items.summary_raw: Leptin Receptor-expressing (LepR + ) stromal cells in the bone marrow are a critical source of growth factors for the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and most restricted hematopoietic progenitors. An important unresolved question is whether they also regulate terminal differentiation in some hematopoietic cells. We found that bone marrow LepR + cells promote thrombopoiesis by synthesizing the chemokine CXCL14. Cxcl14 -expressing LepR + cells extend fine processes that wrap around perisinusoidal megakaryocytes. Deletion of Cxcl14 from LepR + cells did not significantly alter HSC function or most aspects of bone marrow hematopoiesis, including megakaryocyte generation; however, it significantly reduced the numbers of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and platelets in the blood, as well as platelet quality. Megakaryocytes from Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice expressed lower levels of genes that encode granule proteins as compared to control mice, leading to the release of platelets with fewer α-granules and defective thrombus formation/growth. CXCL14 promoted platelet formation by remodeling lipid metabolism in megakaryocytes, increasing fatty acid transporter expression and enabling megakaryocytes to take up more polyunsaturated fatty acids from circulation. A high fat diet rescued the formation of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes and platelets, as well as platelet function, in Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice. CXCL14 protein was sufficient to…

items.title: Direct CO 2 splitting using light-based catalysis and an oxygen reservoir
items.summary_raw: As the dominant anthropogenic greenhouse gas, the conversion of CO 2 into value-added products is vital for achieving a circular economy. CO 2 activation typically requires coreactants, high temperatures, or significant electrical input, any of which increases cost or limits scalability. Here we demonstrate a straightforward way to split CO 2 directly into carbon monoxide and oxygen using light. By combining a light-driven antenna-reactor photocatalyst with a material that acts as an oxygen reservoir, CO 2 can be decomposed directly into CO and oxygen with light only. Under illumination, photoexcited carriers induce CO 2 bond dissociation, while cerium oxide adsorbs the released oxygen into vacancy sites, preventing recombination. The oxygen can then be released from the ceria by flowing nitrogen under white light illumination, a process that can be repeated multiple times, restoring full photocatalytic activity. This demonstrates a practical and scalable strategy for efficient CO 2 conversion, shifting the chemical equilibrium of CO 2 dissociation in a controllable manner.

items.title: Automating inequality? Gender bias in AI-mediated labor markets
items.summary_raw: Generative AI is rapidly entering labor markets, with large language models (LLMs) now used to help write CVs and evaluate applicants. We study the risks this creates in a series of audit experiments in which applicant gender is randomly assigned while all other information is held constant. We find that LLMs generate gender-stereotypical CVs and exhibit gender bias in screening scores and wage recommendations. Screening scores track occupational gender segregation, penalizing women in male-dominated occupations and favoring them in female-dominated ones. Wage recommendations track occupational gender wage gaps when gender is explicit in the prompt, though this gradient weakens under name-based gender signaling and is sensitive to the LLMs being used. These disparities arise through two channels: evaluation bias, when identical CV content is evaluated differently by gender, and generation bias, when gendered content produced by the model affects later evaluation. Because the same systems shape both CV content and its subsequent assessment, these channels can reinforce one another. Taken together, our findings identify measurable risks of algorithmic amplification in AI-mediated job search.

items.title: Supercritical snapping and controlled launching via dual-latch gels
items.summary_raw: Natural organisms have evolved integrated Latch-Mediated Spring Actuation systems (LaMSA) that consist of multiple latches and springs to enhance power output and adapt to diverse environmental conditions. Similar designs are appealing yet largely unexplored in engineered materials due to the complexity of integrating multiple components into a single material platform. Here, we report a dual-latch magneto-elastic shell device capable of selectively activating the latches to regulate snapping pathways and energy output based on specific actuation requirements. Differential deswelling across the thickness acts as the “motor” to load the elastic energy into the shell, which is then released via the snap-through instability once the loading reaches the critical threshold, constituting an intrinsic mechanical latch. Activation of the external magnetic latch delays snapping onset beyond the threshold of the intrinsic latch, leading to a power-amplified supercritical snap-through instability as well as a bifurcation instability. The combined function of both latches allows for flexible control over energy storage and release. Additionally, this integrated LaMSA system possesses an untethered anchoring mechanism, enabling the device to launch in arbitrary directions from the substrate, driven by the energy released during snapping. We envision that the design principles of dual-latch LaMSA systems will create opportunities for power-dense actuation in engineered materials and…

items.title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions
items.summary_raw: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC–HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC–HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure–temperature ( P-T ) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC–HCP phase boundary places the…

items.title: Distinct nanoscale architectures of GABAergic inhibitory synapses predict diverse synaptic output
items.summary_raw: GABAergic synaptic inhibition is heterogenous across neuronal compartments, and plays a critical role in shaping local, cellular, and circuit excitability. In pyramidal neurons, inhibition is mediated by GABA A receptors (GABA A Rs) clustered at the inhibitory postsynaptic domain (iPSD). Synaptic strength depends not only on the number of GABA A Rs within the iPSD, but also on their precise nanoscale organization into discrete subsynaptic domains (SSDs). These SSDs often align with presynaptic GABA release sites to form nanocolumn structures that enhance synaptic efficacy. While nanocolumn organization is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of synaptic function, most studies of GABAergic synapses have focused on archetypal dendritic synapses, which control the plasticity and integration of excitatory inputs. Nonetheless, it remains unclear whether somatic synapses—which deliver robust inhibition to suppress neuronal output—share a similar nanoarchitecture. Here, we used complementary superresolution imaging approaches to directly compare inhibitory synapses in somatic and dendritic compartments. We found that somatic synapses are larger and exhibit greater structural diversity and nanoscale complexity than dendritic synapses. Dendritic synapses display relatively compact architectures with GABA A R SSDs frequently arranged into nanocolumns. In contrast, somatic synapses show a broader range of organizations, including aligned nanocolumns as well as more disorganized…

items.title: Correction for Oveson and Gumel, Projected effects of removing school-entry vaccination requirements on measles transmission in Florida
Sustainability of violence prevention after a randomized vacant lot greening intervention in Philadelphia: A 10-y follow-up
items.summary_raw: Vacant lot greening has been shown to reduce violence and crime in the short-term [C. C. Branas et al. , Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 115 , 2946–2951 (2018)]. We assessed the 10-y impact of a 2013 clustered randomized controlled trial (RCT) of lot greening in Philadelphia on violence and crime. We measured lot greening by treatment assignment from the original 2013 cluster RCT and a longitudinal greening score to assess the sustainability of the treatment assignment from 2012 through 2023. Our outcomes were the annual reported total crime, violent crime, and firearm violent crime per square mile at each lot. We conducted intent-to-treat and contamination-adjusted intent-to-treat analyses to estimate the local average treatment effect on relative change in crime. Lots randomized to the full greening intervention remained greener over time compared to other lots. In intent-to-treat analyses, compared to lots that received no intervention, lots that received any intervention had a 9% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.96) and a 9% decrease in violent crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.97) per square mile per year. In contamination-adjusted analyses, compared to lots without sustained greening treatment, lots with sustained greening treatment had a 12% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.88, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.93) and an 11% decrease in density of violent crime (estimate = 0.89, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.95) per square mile per year. items.title: Correction for Tan et al., PLD1-driven oncogenic secretion creates a therapeutic vulnerability in chromosome 3q–amplified NSCLC
Behind stable richness, more European pollinators are losing than gaining
Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
items.summary_raw: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth’s surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.

items.title: China’s energy transition strategy favoring both coal and renewables: Economic risks and global implications
items.summary_raw: China’s energy strategy is navigating a complex policy landscape: While leading the world in renewable energy manufacturing and deployment, it is simultaneously pursuing a continued expansion of its coal-fired power fleet. This paper examines this dual trajectory by building an integrated analytical framework that combines domestic and international perspectives to analyze the social, economic, climate, and geopolitical impacts of China’s new coal-power plant investments. Combining historical trends, government planning, and projections from influential policy teams, we find that a tripling of renewable capacity by 2030, a pace China is on track to meet, is sufficient to satisfy all projected electricity demand scenarios when considered alongside the evolving generation mix and planned storage deployment. We further show that additional coal capacity is not required to ensure adequate electricity supply under these scenarios. The coal pathway could expose up to $223.6 billion of stranded assets from new projects and add an additional 327,000 workers in a declining industry. Furthermore, this trajectory may weaken the alignment between China’s domestic energy investment and its international clean energy leadership. We conclude that a clean-energy-led pathway that halts new coal construction is lower-cost, better for job growth, and more consistent with China’s role as a leader in the global clean energy transition.

items.title: No evidence for a universal effect of writing on language use or the evolution of syntax
items.summary_raw: The acquisition of writing has a lasting effect on how languages are processed in the brain, raising the possibility that it also affects how they are used and evolve over time. A popular hypothesis is that writing specifically leads to the increased use and evolution of complex hierarchical structures in language. While most case studies on individual languages have supported this, it remains unclear whether results scale to larger and more diverse sets of languages. Here we test this prediction in two ways: 1) synchronically, by modeling the effect of modality (written vs. nonwritten) on syntactic complexity, operationalized via hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences, in corpora from 30 languages; and 2) diachronically, by modeling whether the development of writing affected the phylogenetic dynamics of hierarchy in clause combinations across 59 languages from three families. We found no effect of writing on the response variables in either analysis. Hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences do not demonstrably differ between spoken and written use of language, and the introduction of writing had no discernible effect on the evolution of clause combinations in grammar. There is weak evidence for a decrease in variance in structural asymmetry after the introduction of writing in one family, possibly reflecting the impact of increased normativity. Our findings challenge popular beliefs about the relationship between writing and hierarchy and suggest that…

items.title: Gaplinc regulates myeloid metabolic pathways in trans in endotoxic shock
items.summary_raw: The long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) Gaplinc is a known regulator of the innate immune response; however, the systemic mechanisms governing its influence on survival during endotoxic shock remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Gaplinc as a dosage-dependent immune and metabolic rheostat. While Gaplinc knockout (KO) mice exhibit elevated baseline immune response genes (IRGs) and resistance to lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced shock, we demonstrate that transgenic Gaplinc overexpression produces the opposite phenotype: suppressed baseline IRGs, diminished nuclear p65, and hypersensitivity to endotoxemia. Analysis of heterozygous and rescue models reveals that Gaplinc functions in trans and is haploinsufficient, requiring strict transcript dosage to maintain wild-type immune homeostasis. To uncover the mechanistic basis of this survival advantage, we performed RNA Antisense Purification (RAP-MS) and identified the mitochondrial enzyme MCCC1 as a primary Gaplinc binding partner. Loss of Gaplinc drives systemic metabolic reprogramming, characterized by reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and a protective lipidome featuring elevated lysophosphatidylcholines and diminished free fatty acids. Finally, while myeloid-specific conditional KOs confer partial protection against LPS-induced hypothermia, tissue-wide expression mapping and sex-dimorphic clinical chemistries suggest a broader, multisystemic role for the lncRNA. Collectively, these data demonstrate that Gaplinc…

items.title: Peak water: Trends in decoupling regional and global water use
items.summary_raw: Water use for human activities, including food and fiber production, energy generation, and residential, commercial, and industrial supply, has grown significantly over the past century, driven by rising populations, expanding economic activity, and changes in technologies and consumer demands. Traditional water planning has long assumed that the demand for water, like other resource demands, will grow in perpetuity, shaping infrastructure development, land-use decisions, and water-system investments. However, recent data and analysis challenge this assumption, suggesting that total water use in certain regions and sectors has peaked or even begun to decline, despite continued population and economic growth. This paper’s primary contribution is to reevaluate the status of “peak water” and decoupling based on observational and statistical data, as well as multimodel simulations. Data on global, national, and regional water withdrawals indicate that certain peak water-use levels are being reached and the paper discusses past, current, and projected demand estimates; potential drivers of observed water use reductions; and different strategies for managing and modeling water use in the future. These findings indicate that the long-presumed correlation between water-resource use, economic development, and human well-being can be decoupled and that models of water use should reflect this. Decoupling solutions must focus on efficiency technologies, regulatory water-use caps…

items.title: Surfing sequence landscapes with sequence–structure augmentation
Calculated residue protonation states find functional, conserved E-channel proton-loading sites in Complex I from bacteria to mammals
items.summary_raw: Bioenergetic proton pumps take protons from one side of a membrane, transiently binding them at a loading site within the protein matrix, and then release them to the other side against an electrochemical gradient. The E channel of Complex I, from bacteria to mammals, contains a conserved proton-loading region whose function is distributed among several interacting residues. Noting extensive sequence divergence across homologous Complex I structures, we asked how this function is conserved during evolution despite many amino acid changes. Multi-Conformation Continuum Electrostatics (MCCE) calculations were performed on the five E-channel subunits from 41 experimental structures from bacteria, cyanobacteria, insects, and mammals. A Monte Carlo sampling identified five to seven residues in each species that function as a proton-loading cluster. Structures with a closed E-channel have ~1 more proton in the cluster than those with open conformations. Proton binding represents ensemble averages across thousands of accessible microstates, each with an integer protonation state. A mean-field analysis showed that the proton affinity depends on both titrating residues and the surrounding protein electrostatic environment. Closely related proteins use nearly the same cluster of residues, whereas more divergent proteins substitute alternative proton-handling residues and modify electrostatically important fixed-charge groups to preserve cluster proton affinity. items.title: How Social Media Became a Permitting Reform Battleground
items.summary_raw: If you occupy the same corner of the internet as I do (hello over there), you may have noticed a lot of posts about the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act — not just from Hill-watchers and energy wonks, but by creators and influencers on Instagram. “I’ve watched the same anti-BAAJA video at least 16 times,” Kaitlyn Hennessy, a creator who tracks influence campaigns, posted on Instagram on Wednesday, referring to a wave of substantially similar videos attacking the bill. These videos typically include a detailed critical description of one or several of the bill’s provisions followed by a “call to action,” such as contacting a congressional representative. Though they appear at first blush to be standard activist fare, at least some are in fact part of paid influencer campaigns led by environmental NGOs or other advocacy groups. “The prevalence of social media posts regarding BAAJA — both for and against — has all of the hallmarks of a paid and coordinated campaign,” Hennessy told me in an email. “They have shockingly similar talking points about complicated legislation, the same call-to-actions, many posted at the same time, and with repetitive talking points.” Influencers and creators are appealing messengers for issue advocacy and political campaigns. items.title: Climate change adaptation in the Philippines: a systematic review of empirical evidence
items.summary_raw: Abstract Highly climate-vulnerable countries face the dual challenge of responding to growing climate hazards while addressing the social and institutional conditions that shape vulnerability and adaptation. National evidence syntheses are needed to assess how adaptation research is progressing and whether it provides evidence about the outcomes of adaptation responses. We examine these questions in the Philippines, where climate exposure intersects with livelihood precarity, social vulnerability, and uneven institutional capacity. We conducted a systematic review of empirical evidence on human climate change adaptation in the Philippines and identified 99 relevant studies published between 2010 and 2024. We analysed their research themes and empirical findings, together with the subset directly assessing adaptation outcomes or effectiveness. The literature predominantly examines perceptions, adaptive capacity, and sectoral responses, particularly in fisheries, coastal settings, and agriculture. Over time, research has broadened from local vulnerability, coastal risk, and household coping toward institutional capacity, managed retreat, social capital, justice, and equity. However, only 13 studies directly evaluated adaptation outcomes. These studies found that adaptation can improve yields, food security, housing, safety, and local resilience, but that benefits depend on markets, technical support, institutional capacity, and fair implementation. items.title: Bedrock Energy Raises $24 Million to Mainstream Small-Scale Geothermal
items.summary_raw: Geothermal energy has been one of the clearest bipartisan winners of the second Trump administration’s energy policy. But the attention has largely centered on companies like Fervo Energy and Sage Geosystems, which aim to generate electricity from hot rocks often miles beneath the surface. Now, a less-heralded corner of the geothermal industry is attracting notice: ground source heat pumps, which use the stable underground temperature of the Earth to heat and cool buildings. Texas-based startup Bedrock Energy is trying to modernize geothermal HVAC, a technology that dates back to the 1940s but still only serves about 1% of single-family homes and roughly 0.3% to 0.5% of large commercial buildings. High upfront drilling costs and space constraints have hampered adoption, as conventional systems typically require dozens or even hundreds of shallow wells spread across a sizable footprint. Bedrock just raised $24 million to scale a different approach, using AI and an array of sensors to drill fewer, deeper, and cheaper wells more quickly than ever before. The basic idea behind geothermal heating and cooling is that once you get just a few hundred feet below the surface, the Earth stays at a relatively steady temperature year-round, typically between 50 and 70 degrees Fahrenheit. Geothermal heat pumps circulate fluid through a network of underground pipes, drawing heat from the ground to warm buildings in winter and depositing excess indoor heat underground in summer. items.title: Carbon dioxide is a climate problem. It might also be a laundry solution.
items.summary_raw: Doing the laundry has grown easier and more efficient over the years, yet two things have always remained the same: A washing machine needs water, and a dryer needs heat. Technology designed to clean aerospace parts reimagines the process by ditching both of those in favor of an unlikely substitute: carbon dioxide, the very gas we’re trying so hard to contain. Under pressure, CO2 becomes a low-viscosity liquid capable of penetrating fabrics and carrying away oils and grime. When depressurized, it reverts to a gas, leaving clothes clean and dry. No wastewater. No dryer. Beyond its novelty, the idea could clean up a resource-intensive chore. The average family runs roughly 300 loads a year, consuming thousands of gallons of water. And more than 80 percent of U.S. households own a dryer, with one study putting the annual CO2 emissions from machine drying alone at 27 million metric tons . Long confined to industrial operations, liquid-CO2 cleaning is getting a second look from appliance giants LG and Samsung — this time for the home. Still, shrinking a technology built around bulky, high-pressure machinery to fit both a laundry room and household budget is a tall order. No less challenging is doing so without washing away the environmental gains that make waterless, dryerless laundry so enticing in the first place. Just getting this far has taken decades. Corporate Carbon Footprint Disclosure in the Audiovisual Industry: A Global Assessment Using the Carbon Integrity Index
items.summary_raw: Media companies are experts at communicating climate change to the public, yet it is unclear whether they apply the same rigor when reporting their own carbon footprint. The Carbon Integrity Index (CIX), a peer-reviewed 10-indicator index of emissions reporting quality, was applied to the audiovisual industry for the first time. Of the 26 audiovisual companies with revenues above USD 2000 million, 21 published emissions data. Each was scored in two independent assessments, one manual and one AI-assisted with full human review, and discrepancies were resolved by the evaluators, with a CIX specialist mediating when they disagreed. Despite their communication expertise, their own reporting was weak and uneven: the mean score was 5.24 (grade D+, weak), and six companies received the lowest grade (D−). Nineteen did not report the uncertainty of their figures, and none disaggregated its emissions by activity center. Disclosure of value-chain emissions was of similar quality to that of operational emissions, but weaker when employee mobility was excluded. Disclosure quality differed significantly between regions, with European companies scoring highest, whereas neither company size nor public ownership was associated with it. This suggests that disclosure quality depends more on each company and its regional context than on its resources.

Pokud však nastanou příznivé podmínky, dokážou vzhledem ke své velikosti růst rychleji než dospělé stromy. Ukázal to výzkum , na kterém se v rámci Ústavu výzkumu globální změny AV ČR-Czechglobe podíleli naši kolegové ve spolupráci také s vědci z Výzkumného ústavu pro krajinu a při kterém byl sledován růst stromů ve čtyřech přírodě blízkých lesích. Výsledky mohou přispět ke zpřesnění modelů budoucího vývoje lesů, jejich obnovy a schopnosti ukládat uhlík v podmínkách klimatické změny. Více píše ekolist.cz zde.

items.title: Green hydrogen in the energy transition: integrating technology, economics, and deployment through a multi-dimensional framework
items.summary_raw: Green hydrogen has emerged as a strategic option for decarbonizing sectors in which direct electrification remains technically or economically constrained. However, technological advances in electrolysis do not necessarily translate into viable large-scale deployment, which depends on broader economic, resource, infrastructure, application, and institutional conditions. This study presents a structured, evidence-based literature synthesis supported by bibliometric analysis to identify the conditions and system-level interactions governing green hydrogen deployment. Using Methodi Ordinatio, 9625 records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection were screened and prioritized, resulting in a final corpus of 120 articles organized into four thematic clusters: fundamentals, applications, techno-economic feasibility, and technological innovations. Bibliometric and thematic analyses reveal a research landscape strongly concentrated on electrocatalysis, electrolyzer performance, and renewable-powered electrolysis, while infrastructure, sectoral integration, and broader deployment conditions remain comparatively less represented. To bridge this gap, a multi-dimensional analytical framework integrating six interdependent dimensions, technology, economics, resources, infrastructure, applications, and policy and governance, was developed and operationalized through a semi-quantitative decision-support procedure. An illustrative hybrid solar-wind hydrogen scenario demonstrates…

items.title: All it takes is political will? Political agency, cabinet governance and climate regulations
items.summary_raw: Why do some governments adopt stringent climate policies despite the electoral risks? While existing research emphasises the role of institutions in enabling ambitious climate action, it often overlooks the agency of elected politicians in navigating intra-cabinet conflicts and how different modes of bargaining affect policy output. Taking the case of the housing sector, where climate policy costs can spark backlash, this article examines how cabinet governance, especially mechanisms of conflict resolution, shapes the adoption of stringent climate regulations. Applying process tracing to Germany’s heating law to phase out fossil fuel heating (2023) and France’s minimum energy performance standards for rentals (2021), the study finds two different pathways through which the agency of politicians enables stringent climate policy. The article contributes to the literature by providing a more granular account of how institutions such as cabinet governance shape policy outcomes by conditioning the strategies available to elected politicians.

items.title: From Eco-Despair to Optopia: Climate Catastrophe and Planetary Survival in Kim Stanley Robinson's The Ministry for the Future
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: Contemporary fiction is dominated by apocalyptic dystopias and eco-despair. Kim Stanley Robinson'snovel The Ministry for the Future (2020) explores the themes of eco-despair and climate anxiety associatedwith the Holocene extinction, resulting in dystopian consequences in the Anthropocene. The novel bridgesthe present and a future in which the effects of climate change are mitigated, and the Holocene extinctionis halted. This novel has been described as antidystopian rather than utopian and realistic at its core. Thisarticle examines how Robinson uses narrative realism to address real economic, political, and ecologicalissues. Robinson introduces the term Optopia, meaning an optimum utopia: a world that is imperfect yetrealistic and that shifts from speculative fiction towards pragmatic survival. The novel opens with aheatwave in India that stands as a symbol of ecological disruption; later, it shifts its narrative focus to theglobal institutions and how the global institutions establish the Ministry for the Future. The paperexamines the darker side of ecological transition, evaluates the role of ecoterrorism and the ethicalcompromises necessary to maintain ecological governance. Finally, this article argues that The Ministry forthe Future serves as an ecocritical intervention in the Anthropocene. It presents climate fiction not as adoomsday warning, but as a realistic manual for planetary survival.This study adopts a qualitative and ecocritical approach to analyze Kim…

items.title: From Tin Crisis to Thorium Transition: Energy Justice, Youth Acceptance, and Participation in Bangka Belitung’s Nuclear Future
items.summary_raw: Bangka Belitung, Indonesia’s tin heartland, entered a compound crisis in 2024: provincial economic growth slowed to 0.77% after a crackdown on corruption in the tin trade, while about 167,000 hectares of land remain critically degraded. In 2025 the province also received Indonesia’s first regulatory approval for a nuclear power project, a site-evaluation program for a 500-megawatt thorium molten salt reactor on Kelasa Island. This study asks under what conditions youth acceptance of the project would be just and how acceptance could become participation in its governance. Using a qualitative explanatory case study that combines an integrative literature review with document analysis of regulatory, statistical, industry, and media sources, it evaluates four theoretical propositions through pattern matching. The evidence shows that the regulator has demonstrated technical rigor but procedural inclusion remains thin; that local support is driven mainly by expected economic benefits under conditions of crisis; that benefit-sharing arrangements remain undefined; and that the only site-specific acceptance survey predates the crisis and was co-authored by developer staff. The youth research team therefore designed a Youth Energy Justice Lab linking project benefits to ex-mining land restoration and youth-led monitoring.

items.title: Taking people with you? How MPs interpret their electoral mandate on climate change
items.summary_raw: This article explores how MPs interpret their electoral mandate when a policy issue becomes electorally contested. MPs’ self-conceptions of electoral accountability, as distinct from their behavioural strategies, have received little qualitative attention. Drawing on 63 interviews with cross-party MPs in the UK and Germany (2023–2024), and using climate change as a case, this article reconstructs how representatives reason about electoral sanction. Following a most-different systems design, it finds that MPs’ understandings of their mandate divide along two distinct lines rather than a single ideological one. The first - whether ‘taking people with you’ means leading opinion or accommodating it - cuts across both party and country. The second - whether electoral sanction is treated as legitimate democratic feedback or an obstacle to effective policy - is more country-inflected, though with notable within-country variation. The article contributes a qualitative account of how MPs interpret electoral accountability in contested policy fields.

items.title: Off-grid living as a primary data gap: Motivations, challenges, and policy implications in Queensland
items.summary_raw: Australia leads the world in the proportion of distributed (household-level) solar PV. Over four million Australians have installed rooftop solar PV, and an increasing number of households are investing in domestic battery energy storage. As these technologies become more accessible, popular, and affordable, a growing number of households may choose to disconnect from the centralised grid. Despite this possibility, little is known about off-grid households, including their experiences, motivations for transitioning off-grid, and the challenges they encounter. This paper explores the lived experiences of off-grid households in Queensland, the Australian state with the highest number of installed PV systems and an engaged community of off-grid residents. Using the theoretical lens of ‘critical data studies’, we conceptualise off-grid households as a context, in which there is a ‘primary data gap’. We conclude with a discussion of policy implications and propose recommendations, emphasising that the absence of data on off-grid households is not neutral – it actively shapes policy in ways that may disadvantage them.

items.title: Progress, ambition and gaps towards the 2030 EU27 climate and energy targets
items.summary_raw: This study examines the alignment, progress, and ambition of EU27 Member States in meeting the 2030 targets for greenhouse gas reductions, renewable energy deployment, and energy efficiency improvements, as reported in their National Energy and Climate Plans. The analysis applies a gap approach and is framed within debates on renewable energy securitisation, EU climate leadership, and the ‘energy efficiency first’ principle. Results show that most Member States display insufficient ambition across the three areas compared to EU benchmarks. The EU’s leadership-by-example approach is evident in Sweden, Romania, and Lithuania, which have achieved long-term GHG reductions, and in Greece and Hungary, which show progress under the Effort Sharing Regulation. The securitisation of renewables is clear in countries near Russia. In energy efficiency, the analysis highlights ongoing challenges. Only a few Member States are on track to fulfil 2030 commitments, while for most the targets appear overly ambitious given current performance.

items.title: Broadcast time in the age of acceleration: Media archaeology, environmental authority and David Attenborough
items.summary_raw: David Attenborough’s authority as an environmental witness has proved unusually durable, repeatedly reaffirmed within a media culture structured by acceleration and attention scarcity. That persistence owes less to celebrity visibility, persuasive messaging or advocacy than to media temporality, specifically the broadcast natural-history documentary as a form organised by return, repetition, and institutional trust. Innis’s distinction between time- and space-biased media, McLuhan’s account of media as perceptual environments and Arendt’s separation of authority from persuasion frame David Attenborough: A Life on Our Planet as a ‘witness statement’ that makes duration its primary communicative resource. By binding ecological change to an embodied lifetime, archival return and recurring indices, the film opposes a long horizon of judgement to the short cycles of circulation characteristic of algorithmic platform infrastructures. Climate communication often produces fatigue because the temporal preconditions for authority, including continuity, shared reference points and durable institutions, are increasingly difficult to sustain. The article contributes to climate communication research by reframing environmental authority as a media-temporal condition rather than as an effect of persuasion, celebrity visibility or audience response. Attenborough’s case is therefore less a model to replicate than a limit case in which such recognition can still be inherited.

items.title: Relationship between project delivery system and historic nuclear power plant construction performance in the United States
Decolonising climate resilience: an analysis of older women’s roles as food producers, caregivers and climate agents in rural Zimbabwe
items.summary_raw: This article employs decolonial and feminist political economy lenses to understand the role of older women in climate change mitigation, adaptation and resilience in rural Zimbabwe. The article is based on a qualitative research methodology to comprehend the subjective narratives of 12 older women selected from Umzingwane district in Matabeleland South province. The article argues that older women play a critical role as they are food producers, caregivers and agents in climate resilience initiatives. Older women are the main agents in food systems, particularly in seed preservation, subsistence farming and processing. On caregiving, older women often care for children and other family members during and after climate crisis; they manage household nutrition and diminishing resources and provide mental and emotional labour in times of crisis. Older women are adaptation agents as they lead in providing innovative adaptation strategies, such as shifting planting times and cultivating resilient crop varieties, and shape household decision-making processes. While the role of older women in climate resilience is undervalued, it is critical for the survival of rural households during and after climate change crisis. As such, the article suggests decolonising climate resilience discourses through recognition of the role of older women in climate change resilience, valuing and incorporating older women into broader decision-making platforms.

items.title: What Makes People Vote for the Greens? Social Structure, Ideological Conflict Lines and the East–West Divide in Germany
items.summary_raw: This paper looks at East–West differences in electoral support for the Greens in Germany. While previous research has examined the electorate of the Greens with focus on socio-structural patterns, or environmental concern, the literature lacks investigations into the long-standing and increasing East–West divide in Green voting. Based on data from the European Social Survey (ESS round 11, 2023), we use blockwise binary logit regressions to investigate whether East–West differences can be explained by social structure and attitudes on contemporary ideological cleavages. Results reveal that the East–West difference in voting for the Greens can be entirely attributed to differences in climate change concern. Further analyses indicate that climate change concerns are not more salient for Eastern than for Western German voters at the polls, but that the level of climate change concern is higher among Eastern Germans. Our analysis adds to recent research on explaining the Green vote and research on an East–West divide in Germany.

items.title: Break‐Even Conditions for HTS‐HVDC in Constrained High‐Capacity Renewable‐Energy Transmission Corridors
items.summary_raw: Constrained transmission corridors motivate comparison of high‐temperature superconducting high‐voltage direct‐current (HTS‐HVDC) with conventional VSC‐HVDC under a common receiving‐end service and contingency requirement. This study links three questions: how transmission ratings determine installed reserve, how much additional conventional corridor capital is required for parity and what conductor procurement price permits parity. The calculation purchases complete cable, converter and cooling inventories for independent modules and evaluates lifecycle expenditure and delivered energy. A 2‐GW conventional reference is compared with 2‐, 3‐, 4‐ and 5‐GW HTS planning modules using a common converter–cost relationship. At 2.1 GW receiving‐end power and 500 km, the additional conventional capital required for parity is approximately USD 0.80 billion for equal‐2‐GW modules and USD 1.39 billion for 5‐GW HTS modules. Fewer HTS assemblies can therefore coincide with a higher cost of installed reserve. Conductor‐price thresholds depend on that architecture and the assumed additional‐corridor capital; three heat‐ingress scenarios show their thermal sensitivity. Reliability and input uncertainty qualify these conditions rather than establish commercial feasibility. The calculations use published component correlations and explicit author cost and reliability scenarios. Historical project comparisons do not validate the conventional coefficients, and conductor‐current evidence does not…

items.title: Staying under climate change: review of drivers, outcomes and intersectional dimensions of immobility
items.summary_raw: Climate change is increasingly framed as a driver of human migration, yet migration is not a universal response to climate stress. Many individuals and households remain in place despite climatic, economic, and social risks, raising important questions about why people stay, under what conditions, and with what consequences. This paper undertakes an exploratory review of the literature on human immobility in the context of climate change. It addresses a gap in existing scholarship, which has often examined trapped populations, voluntary staying, gendered immobility, or livelihood outcomes separately, through case-based studies, without systematically synthesising the drivers, outcomes, and intersectional dimensions of immobility together. Drawing on cross-disciplinary literature across migration studies, climate change adaptation, human geography, disaster studies, and development research, the paper argues that staying is not merely the absence of migration, but a dynamic and socially produced process shaped by both agency and constraint. Environmental, social, economic, institutional, and psychological drivers interact to shape decisions to stay, and produce outcomes ranging from livelihood stability, social cohesion, and in-situ adaptation; to poverty, care burdens, psychosocial stress, and heightened risk exposure. These processes are socially differentiated by gender, age, class, caste, race, and intra-household relations. We suggest using the term “staying” in place of…

items.title: Decarbonizing residential buildings: Evaluating heat pump solar and battery renovation pathways
Vocabularies on Climate and Housing Justice from a Landfill in Bhalswa, New Delhi, India
items.summary_raw: Cities of the Global South are at the forefront of the climate and environmental crisis, where climate change acts as a threat multiplier on existing social, economic, political and spatial inequalities. This paper asks how to frame and address the climate crisis amidst long-standing housing inequalities in the Global South, through the case of housing for waste workers adjacent to the Bhalswa landfill in Delhi, India. Various housing typologies exist adjacent to Bhalswa and are shaped by tenure precarity, inadequate basic services, and direct exposure to landfill fires, groundwater contamination and debris, even as access to the landfill remains central to residents' livelihoods. Drawing on a year-long ethnographic study of health histories with 15 waste-worker households, we argue that residents articulate climate and housing vulnerability through their own vocabulary rather than the technical language of climate science. We trace four Hindi words that recurred across our interviews-Khatā (the landfill as place), kām (work), Kirāyā (rent), and jhelnā (to endure) as an emplaced register for naming climate change, not a translation of it. The paper argues that housing and climate justice cannot be addressed separately in the Global South, and that vocabulary-building is itself a form of epistemic and political recognition.

items.title: No matter how you ask, more Americans are negative than positive about AI
items.summary_raw: Five high-quality surveys ask about AI in different ways. Their wording matters, but the overall picture is consistent.

items.title: Climate Change and Human-Wildlife Conflict: A Case of Berejena in Chivi District, Zimbabwe
items.source_name: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
items.summary_raw: Climate change often affects the harmonious coexistence of humans and wildlife.This qualitative study assessed the impact of climate change on human-wildlife relationships in Berejena.The researchers interviewed a convenient sample of 10 participants and thematically analyzed the collected data.This study established that the climate in Berejena has changed, now characterized by erratic rainfall and high temperatures, leading to resource depletion.This triggered wildlife to move into human territories, causing havoc to crops, livestock, and humans themselves.Humans are also forced to encroach on wildlife areas for resources.The study concluded that climate change has precipitated human-wildlife conflict in Berejena.The study therefore underscores the need for policymakers to create policies that address humanwildlife conflict, support habitat restoration projects to rehabilitate degraded ecosystems, provide safe ways to deter wildlife, and promote community education on harmonious coexistence with animals, since they share the same geographical space.

items.title: Hazardous glacial lakes need reservoir governance
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02796-6 Climate warming is expanding thousands of glacial lakes with unstable natural dams, yet high-risk lakes remain outside formal safety oversight despite their potential for downstream harm. These lakes need consequence-based governance analogous to engineered dams and reservoirs, beginning with risk-tiered monitoring and clearer protection during conflict.

items.title: The Politics of Industrial Policy within the Green Division of Labour: Comparing Solar PV Manufacturing in India, Mexico and South Africa
items.summary_raw: There is growing optimism about the possibilities of green industrial policy (GIP), as countries in the Global South deal with the twin challenges of reducing carbon emissions and achieving structural transformation. However, this optimism is founded on a narrow analysis of how the politics of GIP operates. This article calls for critical multi‐scalar political economy analysis to explain GIP outcomes in contexts shaped by earlier phases of neoliberal reform. It takes the case of solar photovoltaics (PV) manufacturing, which is characterized by China's dominance in manufacturing segments of the solar PV chain, to examine how the new politics of green energy transition is shaping GIP outcomes in three large economies that have significantly expanded their solar generation capacity: India, Mexico and South Africa. The article shows how first‐mover countries generate new transnational coalitions around green energy that combine with earlier collaborations forged around neoliberalism to undermine productivist green industrial policy. The resulting prioritization of increasing renewable energy generation above supporting domestic manufacturing ensures the continued subordinate integration of these countries within the green division of labour.

items.title: Renewable Energy’s Comparative Edge over Non-Renewable Energy in Today’s Era and Its Role in the Greenhouse Effect
items.source_name: Journal of Energy and Environmental Sustainability
items.summary_raw: This paper examines whether renewable energy now holds a decisive edge over non-renewable energy in the contemporary era and evaluates how that edge matters for the greenhouse effect. The central argument is that the historical trade-off between environmental performance and economic viability has narrowed sharply, and for a growing share of the electricity sector it has reversed: renewables are no longer only cleaner; many are now cheaper, more modular, more strategically resilient, and more scalable than new fossil-based generation. The study uses a quantitative comparative review design built from recent international datasets and reports, principally from the International Energy Agency (IEA), the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), Ember, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), and the U.S. National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), supplemented by literature on floating solar photovoltaics in India. The paper first documents the present transition context: in 2024, renewables added 585 GW globally and accounted for 92.5% of net power-capacity expansion; renewables supplied a record 32% of world electricity, while clean power including nuclear reached 40.9%. It then compares technology-level life-cycle emissions and costs using formal statistical tests. Renewable electricity technologies in the study sample show a median life-cycle emissions factor of 28 gCO2e/kWh, compared with 840 gCO2e/kWh for fossil technologies. A Welch t-test and a…

items.title: An Ecolinguistic Description of Time Frame in the Grassfields
items.summary_raw: After the COVID-19 pandemic, the world has faced a severe economic crisis followed by an acute environmental degradation. To alleviate the latter, ecology and natural science alone seem insufficient. Temptative solutions from language can be worth exploring. This paper sets out to explore the role of language solving or at least reducing the current global environmental crisis, within a local community in Cameroon, namely the grassfields where one of the dominant languages is Ghomala. In other words, the study aims at unveiling how linguistic elements can be used as a tool to raise consciousness and make people to be attuned back to their environment. To achieve it, the study uses an eclectic approach, combining the ideology approach to ecolinguistics so as to describe the concepts used in the grassfield community to refer to the months of the year and the days of the week, and finally explains how these linguistic concepts are related to activities to be carried out at specific periods in order to preserve the environmental balance. The results show that the days and months carry a semantic and metalinguistic meaning which implicitly orientate the members of the community investigated to carry out activities in congruence with natural balance and nature protection. These findings thus confirm that the languages spoken in certain local communities contain words denoting nature preservation and balance, which can be reactivated in current practices to promote not only…

items.title: Města v horečce
items.summary_raw: Důsledky klimatické změny stále výrazněji pociťujeme i v českých městech. Rostoucí teploty a častější vlny veder ovlivňují každodenní život jejich obyvatel. Ne na všechny ale dopadají stejně. Opatření jako dostatek stínu, stromy nebo zadržování dešťové vody mohou pomoci dopady horka zmírnit. Snaha o jejich zavádění ale často naráží na překážky. O vlnách veder, rostoucích teplotách, ale také pocitových teplotách hovoří Pavel Zahradníček v jednom z díle pořadu České televize Nedej se. K dispozici je v archivu televize zde .

items.title: Climate Resilience as Knowledge-Building: Assessing “Constrained” Local Government Efforts in an Era of Turbulent Federalism
items.summary_raw: State and local governments are navigating a period of turbulent federalism, in which intergovernmental support for sustainability- and resilience-related efforts cannot be relied upon. This field research article explores sustainability and resilience-related planning, implementation, and performance management efforts in constrained municipalities in the U.S. state of Indiana, responding to public administration scholars who have called for advancing theories of managing risks. Drawing from cognitive and collective action theory, we examine these local government sustainability efforts as collective acts of inference or knowledge-building in response to the federal climate policy whiplash from 2021 to 2025 under the Biden and Trump administrations. Evidence suggests that local governments made some progress over the study period in responding to observed climate-related impacts and increasing issue-specific collaborative efforts. However, they made less progress toward preparing for future environmental changes. Given federal funding reversals under presidential administrations, future progress for constrained local governments is uncertain.

items.title: Narratives of salmon production and care in indigenous hatchery programmes
items.summary_raw: Amidst global biodiversity declines, human‐assisted reproduction programmes such as salmon hatcheries are the focus of a highly technical and often fraught debate due to concerns about genetic and ecosystem impacts. Indigenous Peoples in some parts of North America have a vital relationship with salmon, deeply connected with governance, self‐determination, and Treaty rights. However, Indigenous perspectives are largely absent in hatchery literature. We employed a narrative analysis of public‐facing materials produced by Indigenous communities and organizations with hatchery programmes in Canada and the United States, finding three narrative threads that describe: the decline of salmon from pre‐colonial abundance and the adoption of hatcheries in response; the rise of genetic concerns and public controversies; and the role of hatcheries in the context of climate change and accelerating habitat degradation. These findings support a reframing of the hatchery debate towards recognizing distinct Indigenous Knowledge and relationships to hatcheries, alongside efforts to address disparities in power and resources in salmon conservation and stewardship. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.
